It was NOT always like this here. It seems back in the earlier part of the decade, we were encouraged to "Do the Right Thing" and were rewarded for our efforts and risk in a more organic way.

Pros: Good technical environment semiconductor business to expand knowledge base.  Empowered to do experiments as needed, to find answers to ongoing problems.
Cons: Penny pinching.  CEO and executives are focused ONLY on "EPS" Earnings Per Share, and the price of common stock.  After all, this how they grow their personal wealth...through stock options.  Living in constant fear of being sold off or outsourced.  No conferences allowed.  Very little new equipment purchased for our lab.  Seem to be "cooking the books", for years now, to make the division more attractive to potential suitors. Forget about meaningful salary increases.  Many, many years since I saw one of those.

Pros: Work from home though IBM seems to be reducing this option for some positions  Good, dedicated coworkers at the lower levels
Cons: Lack of raises  Lots of talk about customer focus but focus is on $$$ even when it results in significant negative impact to customers  Training provided is only online and primarily sales focused  Repeated layoffs in the U.S.  IBM execs think of employees only as a cost that they want to eliminate.  Everyone is always waiting for the call regardless of performance ratings.  Total lack of respect for employees

Pros: Working at home.  Make 95K sitting home, eating chips, and checking your email every 2 hours.  Another good reason is that IBM looks good on your resume.  Finally, you get really good at dealing with politics and difficult angry people who are this way because they are stressed from being overworked and forced to achieve unrealistic goals.
Cons: Hard to advance career even when you really try hard  and  LOTS of red tape to go through to get anything done.  I always tell people working at IBM is 90% filling out forms / 10% doing actual technical work.  IBM needs to start caring about employees again and we will care about the company.  Until then, we will be unproductive.

Pros: Company offers wide variety of opportunities for different roles, career paths  IF you can get support of your manager.
Cons: Very few opportunities to build interpersonal and team relationships with colleagues and coworkers as most are work from home. Spend lots of time on conference calls with cast of dozens or more. Very slow movement on projects due to "too many cooks," political wrangling and landscape. Difficult to build trust, as many are individual contributors focus on impressing management and rather than focusing on projects that help move the organization forward.

Pros: Smart colleagues, wellrespected company that's a household name, work on challenging and important initiatives, most decisions based on facts and the merits of the argument.
Cons: Bureaucratic and complex. Company does not invest in its employees as much as it used to, pays the minimum to retain employees. You need to be good at setting boundaries because there are major work/life balance issues with expectations that you be connected 24x7. Lack of promotions unless you are politically connected. Feeling of social isolation due to overreliance on technology and conference calls rather than face to face meetings.

Pros: Excellent benfits for employees paired with a generally relaxed environment and very good work/life balance.
Cons: All levels of management like to spout corporate BS about people being assets and looking forward while entire focus is on how much money they can post to Wall St this quarter. This causes many internal tools to fail to work properly as resources are pulled of projects to work on others or just laid off resulting in less efficient working conditions. They are now asking how to keep contractors furloughed to below 40/hrs per week without paying any extra. Raises are still on hold for at least this year, maybe next for contratcors and employees.

Pros: Free parking and being in low traffic location.
Cons: Besides the low pay, this offshore "answer" ends up being the mojo contributing to a culture that exemplifies the many absurdities that might be found in a Dilbert cartoon i.e  on demand seating policy at this facility for instance.  It's Beige Man, in not only the physical surroundings, but in the energy, the vibe, the leadership/management of people.  Creative, Innovative, and statusquo challengers will find it stifling and consistent with the same ole' lumbering bureaucracy where people are just numbers to be manipulated.

Pros: Opportunity to gain true global experience and to meet IT people from many other companies who have been outsourced by IBM.  Opportunity to work with many other large companies and gain the insight of how they run.
Cons: "Resource Actions"/layoffs all the time, never know when your number is up, exempt employees are often expected to work 60 to 80 hours a week and often form months at a time.  Often the job requires travel, still need to do all the work with what hours remain in the week.  Compensation is not that of the competition unless you are a new hire and negotiate real well.  This year the lady running IBM canceled variable pay.

Pros: One of the most enjoyable work environments if you consider fellow employees and cultural diversity. Some of the best engineers and other performers worked their way through the big machine and mostly moved on if they were able to. Solid "B" performers can make a decent, somewhat remunerative career. There are still opportunities and challenges every day.
Cons: Hierarchical, paternalistic, minimal financial incentives. Asinine predetermined evaluation process, which is designed to minimize payroll expense, rather than improve performance.  A mixture of gameplayers and very hard workers managed to maintain course, innovating for a company that only seeks shareholder value at any cost. They've long ago lost the "carrotandstick" approach; taken away all the carrots; it's all stick.

Pros: Absolutely amazing company to work for. The possibilities are truly limitless. The network of support you get just by becoming an IBMer is truly unmatched. Excellent benefits and possibilities of commissions.
Cons: Metrics DDRs are judged on aren’t 100% determined on how hard the rep works. The OTE of $35k/yr. is impossible to calculate ahead of time. It is supposed to be if you get 100% of your quotas then you’ll get the $35k. However, there are reps not getting any of that $35k and reps getting way more. Also it can be very defeating making cold calls/emails with no response, hence not making numbers, and not getting any commission contrary to working hard.

Pros: my teammates who are typically smart and hardworking and frequently considered to be industry experts.  Option to work out of home office was nice.
Cons: Miserable morale and loss of respect for employees.  Shifting people out of the business when their skills and knowledge of how to get things done will be lost forever.  Recent restructuring created many new senior exec jobs just before the Resource Action which eliminated many lower level employees.  Employee's were given low performance ratings to ensure they do not get their bonus on the way out the door, however, senior execs will all get bonuses this year.

Pros: Vast, raw, untapped opportunities abound for your needs for exposure, selfsatisfaction, personal validation, professional breadth and depth of expertise and experiences, and conditioning to not only boringold direct reporting relationships, but REAL and topquality matrix reporting relationships. You can be happy here in 3 ways: personally, professionally and organizationally, and you can do this if you approach IBM as a place where you best contribution is made by figuring out how to squeeze the most of it.
Cons: Do not come here if you think you're going to be led in to everything you need. Do not come here if you have no idea what you need. Seriously, I'm not kidding, GO TO THERAPY before or shortly after coming to IBM to understand what are your personal needslike REALLY your personal needs: are you an introvert, an extrovert, a gogetter, a centrist, a selfdeceiver, a selfvalidator, needy, selfaggrandizing, narcissistic, unsure of yourself, oversure of yourself, etc. etc...only come here if you know what you need. If you don't know, don't come here. Second, don't come here if you don't understand what you could possibly build on your resume in the 1st 100 days. I firmly believe that 1 year at IBM is worth 24 years anywhere else. If you can't put 23 things on your resume in 100 days or less working for IBM, then go back to therapy and see my first point. Lastly, there is no organization to be FOUND at IBM...none. It's flat, with no more than 11%14% of its employees as people managers. IBM's organization lives IN YOUR HEADso get it all up in your head and figure it out. If you are the type of person who needs a very clear organization structure and you freak out without clarity, then please don't come here.

Pros: Good entrylevel opportunity  Infinite wealth of knowledge available to absorb  Very flexible hours
Cons: Extremely difficult to move up or leave a department you can be a victim of your own success and as a result, doors can be closed for you  Hostile review process promotes cutthroat environment with peers If everyone in your team cures a different type of cancer individually, one of you will still get fired for underperforming in comparison with your peers  TOO MANY PROCESSES sometimes you need to create a process to follow a process that has been created to conform to a different process  Too many levels of management. Upper level management never knows what's going on.  Some divisions of IBM are so badly managed that the turnover rate is over 60% GTS for example  NEVER WORK AT A GDF

Pros: You will work with incredibly smart people in IBM. You'll work on really interesting projects. You'll have the ability to change jobs and learn many different parts of the business. IBM is shaping itself to remake enterprise IT for the cloud, harness the power of analytics and big data, and drive applications to follow a systems of engagement paradigm.
Cons: It's a very tough climate internally right now. Constricting budgets, resource actions, minimal raises and benefits eroding slowly over time. Most people want to be at IBM longterm and are holding on for dear life as senior management try to steer the ship to more profitable waters.

Pros: IBM acquired the company I worked for a few years ago.  Surprisingly, the transition into the IBM world was relatively painless, at least for me.  IBM has decent benefits and a good 401k plan.  Many employees work from home, which is a great advantage, saving on commuting time, gas and wear and tear on your car.
Cons: Senior management makes most decisions in a vacuum without regard for the effect it will have on employees and our customers.  Middle management is mediocre at best, with a few shinning stars. There does not seem to be an opportunity to move into other jobs although it's touted that IBM has a career path for employees.

Pros: Well paying career, even for entry level positions  Work from home for many consulting positions  Travel is well compensated and if you can put up with it, you get to experience a lot
Cons: Managerial staff does not pay attention/care about your success at all  To excel, you need experience, but most people are interested in only their development and refuse to help you get said experience  Regarding the last point, hours can be insane, including required weekends. If you travel, say goodbye to a social life, and be sure your relationships can take extreme stress.

Pros: There are mant opportunities to work on large, complex environments the kind if experience it can be difficult to get unless you work for a large software firm. In spite of everything management can do,  there are still some amazing minds at IBM, and many wonderful technicians who are dedicated to their customers success.
Cons: 1 The culture is one if extreme distrust, due in large part to promotion of glad handers and yesmen.  People who actually work hard and are willing to speak truth to power are all too frequently marked for the many layoffs. 2 Far too top heavy. 3 Management far too distracted by industry fads at the expense of customers, employees and the long term health of the business.

Pros: Coworkers and first level and midlevel managers were some of the best and brightest I've worked with. Good teamwork.   Base salary was very good.  Flexible schedules and work from home are commonplace.
Cons: A couple times each year there will be a resource action with layoffs ranging from less than a hundred to multiple thousands. Morale suffers.   Most of my coworkers joined IBM through an acquisition. In other words, most did not choose IBM and apply for an opening there.   IBM delays matching your 401k contributions until Dec. 15, at which time IBM makes a onceayear contribution for the previous twelve months of accrued match. If you leave IBM or IBM lays you off before the company match contribution is made, too bad; you receive $zero match for the entire year; no prorated match.  There are so many silos and divisions that there are duplicate processes.   IBM uses Notes for email and calendar.

Pros: I worked at the Almaden research center and in the Yorktown research center Great research with stateoftheart equipment. Very knowledgeable people, who are also friendly and reliable Still good core values of the IBM company, with people doing their whole 40year career at IBM Personnel encouraged to patent, publish and go to conferences Internal recognition through awards
Cons: Compensation below microelectronics industry average  Hard to obtain information on the technology orientation for future processor generations Company starts to rely too heavily on process improvement rather than disruptive innovation Excessive bureaucracy Recurrent budget restrictions even though IBM Research is highly profitable

Pros: IBM makes a difference in people's lives by applying innovation and technology to create the future. IBM is unique in that it is the only technology company to reinvent itself through multiple technology eras and economic cycles. In 20+ years at the company I have continually found new career opportunities. I have stayed most of all because of the smart, ambitious and talented IBMers I have worked with over the years.
Cons: Given its size and reach IBM can be slow moving. It can be difficult to see one's individual mission as essential to the whole. In a time of industry disruption, the pressure to keep skills relevant is relentless. As IBM moves our clients to the future, we as IBMers must constantly move ourselves to the future as well.

Pros: Good variety of projects and locations. Personnel are friendly and professional. Excellent opportunity to work with technical experts. Flexible schedule and remote opportunities are a big plus.
Cons: For a supposed leader in tech, far too many inefficient processes. Receiving a badge and a login for key systems took way too long after completing a background check and coming on site. Processes for protocols were not transparent and required asking multiple people. The need to call tech support to change a password is incomprehensible and inexcusable.

Pros: Good coworkers, decent pay, good schedule.
Cons: TERRIBLE upper management, AWFUL corporate vision, constant lay off, furloughs, and pay cuts. IBM's corporate vision to make a profit has been to abandon what it was good at and jump on the trendy Cloud Computing   model 5years after Amazon, Google, and Microsoft. IBM is failing so the answer to turn a profit over the last 5 years has been to slash qualified personnel stateside and hire droves of unskilled unqualified workers overseas. Layoffs, pay cuts, and terminating employees close to retirement.

Pros: IBM had a very relaxed environment.  Although I was a cooping for them while finishing my masters degree, the atmosphere was very laid back.
Cons: If you work for IBM for a long time and try to move to another industry, you're in for a little culture shock, most places aren't that laid back compared to IBM.  I know several people who left IBM to work for one of the big finance companies and they went back to IBM to beg for their job back because they couldn't handle the workload and amount of offhour commitments.  Try to keep yourself up to date on technologies and hardware that's going on outside of IBM to avoid becoming a dinosaur.

Pros: Very good coworkers, nice facility. Good place to learn about semiconductor manufacturing and test. Beautiful area of the country in Vermont. Management was good at giving people time off when needed.
Cons: The extremely negative atmosphere made it a very hard place to work. Everybody was stressed out about coming to work and wondering when, not if, the next layoff would occur and who was next on the chopping block. There is and was little to no upper progression for most. The supposed mentoring program was a joke. IBM Burlington is just about the only game in town with decent wages and they know it. Little to no acknowledgement of a job well done. Lack of communication. The type of business is very cyclical with many ups and downs. When the business is down, the first thing they do is get rid of people and equipment.

Pros: You had good team support and training, the vacation and sick policy is very generous, along with some work hour flexibility at times, though getting true product and tools education was mostly a do it yourself project.  But if you worked at it and kept it in front of the manager, you would get it eventually.  One thing I did love was the working environment  very little sniping or backstabbing.  Rather amazing for a large corporate environment.
Cons: Hard to promote up, there often seemed to be a real churn in leaders 1 and 2 levels above you.  Discovered after I left that were was a HUGE variance in pay for people in the same tasks.

Pros: IBM employs  some of the smartest people on the planet. The rank and file, every day non managers are some of the brightest and smartest people you can ever meet.  Very supportive, and highly efficient.
Cons: Once upon a time, IBM was a great company.  Lou Gerstner saved IBM, but at the cost of its corporate soul.  Now IBM, while still a good place to work, but it's only average... Management is no different then any other tech company.... Id go as far as saying it's probably below average hen it comes to management and leadership.

Pros: Ability to switch to different roles and completely different jobs while inside the same company.  Access to leading thinkers and doers across a very VERY broad range of technical and business topics.  Availability of training programs.  Support for volunteer activities in the local community, as well as key programs like Corporate Services Corp where I spend a month with a team of 10 IBMers addressing IT challenges in central Africa.  Respect that comes from association with the IBM brand and history.  Relentless reinvention toward emerging and strategic areas of technology.
Cons: Not as much flexibility for mid/low level managers as their would be in a small organization.  Be aware that skills atrophy will result in minimal compensation increases and eventually needing to locate alternative roles or even company  but this is reality of working in a tech business.

Pros: Good resume filler that’s it
Cons: Management so disconnected from the actual work, truly unbelievable. All they care about is hiring enough people. Placing people in rolls they are prepared for? Nope. Paying people what they are worth? Nope. Overall interest in the employees and their lives outside of work? Nope.  When leaving, my manager told me I was making a “big mistake”. What kind of manager does that? All they would push is the hiring number they had to reach. That’s it, you don’t matter to them at all.  The leader of the office once said “I sometimes forget you guys have families” to us employees at the company picnic. Awesome! Way to reassure me that this place is a terrible work environment.   Terrible training plan, huge disconnect from “core” IBM. Embarrassing to even say I contributed to that office.

Pros: Opportunity for professional growth and advancement, whether you're on a management track or technical track in your career.
Cons: Often though far from always subject to a "one size fits all" mentality when it comes to job role, education/training, etc. Decisions sometimes made/dictated at the highest levels to be applied to everyone with a particular title, often requiring a lot of additional work/overhead with little perceived benefit. People "resources" in the same role/band are not always interchangeable.

Pros: Work Like balance is probably one of the best things IBM has going for it provided that you take advantage of what they are offering.  Otherwise you can get sucked in and commit way too much time to work.
Cons: The promotion system to rating have recently been disconnected allowing them to give praise but hold off on promoting and paying more.  It really boils down to a "trick" to keeping you working for them for less money.  On a different topic IBM is a big company and they say you can move around when you first start.  I would say that this is not always the case.  Depending how the business is doing and your area they will often hold you back.

Pros: Very innovative company with incredible potential. Fairly quick on moving into emerging technologies. Decent education opportunities available to employees even if initial training is terrible.
Cons: The majority of managers are too worried about covering their own butts and only focus on the numbers, so the actual quality of work is terrible. Countless employees with amazing talent are practically forced out of the company due to management not showing recognition for their hard work. New employees are many times left to fend for themselves due to inadequate initial training. Management is so worried about losing back fill spots that they keep incompetent contractors around wasting space instead of working to replace them.

Pros: The pay. Good pay and easy work. I have simple projects with lots of detail. The deadlines are flexible as long as I am making progress. The pay is great but since I am with a contractor, no benefits.
Cons: The lack of job security. One week im secure for years, the next week I am on the chopping block. Very nerve racking. There seems to be always a budget issue. Apparently it is possible to go from contractor status to full time regular status....but we shall see. Also there is no teaching. You need to learn the job yourself or you sink.

Pros: They are RARE, but, if you are lucky, you can find one, MAYBE two IBM managers in a 20+ year career that actually care about the people and are professional.
Cons: What was once a stellar example of reciprocal fidelity and mutual respect and professionality in the 70s/80s is now a maze of backstabbing, obfuscation, doubletalk, and outright lies. No, I wasn't even cut in the "Project Chrome" resource action, but I may end my tenure shortly and by choice. Piece of advice, don't work here, this isn't kneejerk, it's honest. Look elsewhere because I haven't inflated my comments, they are accurate, I am not angry, I am disappointed, and that is far far worse. Find a company that will value and nurture you to give them your absolute best, but don't look here.

Pros: IBM Reputation with existing customers, technology
Cons: Management that is cross pollinated into different divisions where they have no technical expertise to run a business unit. Questions around ethics of management

Pros: IBM is making a deep investment in the data security portfolio. Lots of solid acquisitions QRadar, Big Fix, Resilient Systems Compensation for sales position is competitive. Deep penetration into the fortune 500 with relationships at the very top make large enterprise sales possible. It is possible to reinvent your career at IBM. IBM enables and encourages this.
Cons: Channel sales are a mess. The programs are difficult to understand and even more difficult for business partners to get paid on. Most VAR's in the security space don't work with IBM. This is a huge opportunity missed.  The culture is dated. Too many people who have been at IBM for way too long with dated, unproductive practices. Meetings that result in meetings so they can schedule more meetings.  Healthcare is very expensive for such a large company

Pros: Wide variety of work. Lots of talented people. Opportunity to learn. Design Thinking. A good place to gain experience before you jump to a thriving company. They’ve been around for 100+yearold tech company. Not sure if that’s a pro or a con.
Cons: Soulcrushing executive leadership. Feels like a sinking ship. No 401K match until December so that they don’t pay the match if you leave or get laid off. Insultingly low bonuses. Would be better if they gave you nothing at all. Seeing the CEO grinning while sitting between Donald Trump and Jared Kushner was a source of embarrassment. Although she wasn’t alone.

Pros: There are incredible people  both young and old  here who really care about the success of new hires and clients and the general progress/change of the "old" IBM to the "new". There has always been an ethical leadership aspect to the culture and history of IBM  granted, it's still big corp, but it's clear to me that ethics and security is important to the cloud sales team. There's a wealth of knowledge, resources, and help that the company is willing to invest in the employees. A great starting point for any career to learn about/get exposed to what else is out there while getting advice from both young and old connections in almost any industry.
Cons: Very large company  a lot of moving parts. Slowmoving bureaucracy  official decisions takes a while to solidify and then will change shortly after solidification.

Pros: Benefits, they are still great compared to other Large companies, but slowing losing ground.  Working with a great group of people, it really does feel like a family.  Flexibility to work from home a couple days a week.  I am actually more productive on these days.   Flexibility with work hours, ability to start a little later if needed, or take a long lunch for a doctors / dentist appointment.  Most first line managers are wonderful.  Recognition when a job is well done.  Continual effort in fostering of teamwork.
Cons: The constant fear of 'the job' going over seas.  Upper management is too quick to say yes to every poor idea.

Pros: job security, big company insurance package, ability to move up  but limited.  I met a lot of great people at the job and still keep in touch with them.
Cons: monotonous, "Office Space" movieesque, typical office politics, you are definitely faceless and the management does not have a clean hold on what goes on.  I don't understand how management can make suggestions and implement action plans when they have never picked up the phone and dealt with the problems we had to.  the managers don't even know the equipment.  I made the mistake of ONCE asking for help on a call and the manager looked at me blankly and tried to come up with some kind of answer.  It was oh so very painful.

Pros: Nice environment for supporting outsourced accounts and often able to work at customer sites or remotely. IBM offers competitive salaries and educational opportunities for some positions.
Cons: IBM is one of the leaders in offshoring jobs and if you're in a role that's offshored, you have about a 90% chance of being cut in a resource action.  They target folks who have been around 10 to 15 years and maxed out on salaries. They start by lowering your performance rating without supporting evidence and once that happens, you're history. They supposedly give you an opportunity to find another position in the company but once your names on the cut list, that won't happen.  The folks who stay are chosen based on personality vs performance within the group.

Pros: Tons of things going on, which means opportunities to focus on new interests. Plenty of resources people, books, videos, courses if you are someone who enjoys learning a little every day.
Cons: Constant rumors of layoffs, now with a limited severance program  1 month no matter how many years of service. Raises and bonuses below industry average due to planned sharp declines in revenue and stock buybacks to elevate stock price. This is not a place for those who are anxious about losing their job will thrive due to your being up all night worried about getting let go.

Pros: First 6 months of training in Summit program are great. Learn a lot, challenging, flexible work schedule.  Name recognition.  Relatively good pay. Don't think it is above average though.
Cons: Horrible work culture in the Coppell Sales Center.  Unsanitary work facilities.  Inflexible management around remote work. Required to come in office despite zero valid need to do so.  Siloed view of the rest of IBM.  Lots of workers look well past age of retirement/lots of shuffling around the office. Poor attitudes in older workers  i.e. treats kitchen staff terribly.  Kept at uncomfortably cold temperature. No covered parking for extreme heat or hail storms.  No food or drinks left out for free at any point.

Pros: Can work at home.  Casual dress unless at client and then its do in Rome as the Romans do.  Many possible jobs to change to.  Many different organizations to work in.  More smart people than perhaps any other company.  Great access to research.  Decent benefits.  Try to avoid layoffs.  Great projects to work on.  Always looking to work in the latest technology.
Cons: You can end up with way too much travel.  Travel benefits suck.  Cost savings seem to be more important than revenue growth.  Such a big company makes it hard to find out who knows what.  Many managers are incompetent.

Pros: Flextime is available, but that is almost a standard in the technical world, so I'm not sure it's much of a pro. Lot of smart people to work with, but I've found lots of smart people to work with in other places too. Educational opportunities, but such cost controls that one can never participate in really valuable education.
Cons: No way for advancement without significant job change and likely a relocation. Money is sub par compared to other companies Poor moral due to severe cost controls that hit everything from "thanks" and other  awards to simple team pizza lunches.  Long hours and good work go unrewarded IT equipment is sub par compared to other companies. Lack of resources to do the work. Constant feeling of impending doom as you wait for the outsourcing axe

Pros: You can learn a lot about a lot of different technologies  Challenging projects to manage  Remote work normal
Cons: Can be bureaucratic  Much too much measurement and repeated measurement  Too much overtime 60 hour work week the norm, over 70 sometimes  Not special with treating employees.  Not much "respect for the individual"  Profit is the bottom line not the people  Pressure not to be hit by the next layoff that you know will come, like clockwork

Pros: IBM has a good education program, allowing you to take online courses.  The projects expose you to differing technologies and experiences.  They are a challenge.
Cons: IBM, at least where I am, does not give yearly increases, to my knowledge.  They expect you to bill your maximum hours, and do your online education on your own time. There is a lot of bureaucracy.  I just earned an MBA in Aug 2013 and applied for internal entrylevel consulting positions: everyone I have contacted about those positions has virtually ignored me.  There is a large emphasis on the numbers, but little or no emphasis on rewarding a good job.

Pros: Federal Consulting only: 1. Large programs with national significance.
Cons: 1. Pay is crap. 2. No annual raises  even inflation raises. COLA adjustments don't occur. 3. 12% bonus potential mentioned before getting the job is a fallacy. You will never even get 5%. If you get rated a 1 best, good luck in getting 3%. 4. The way IBM GBS is setup in the public sector, it actually incentivizes one to become a 1099 and work with IBM. In fact  it is great as a subK. 5. Strong smart IBMers leave  unless they're paid well or are IBMers from the "Old Blue". 6. Most IBMers I know have almost never received a raise. In years!

Pros: They do permit full time remote options for full time employees should your work role permit the opportunity.
Cons: It seem you are at the mercy of the clients regardless of if the work makes sense or is reasonable to do. The account managers yes the clients to death and the workers are left to figure out how to make the unrealistic promises come to pass. Prepare to be dumped on a lot. Managers really only seem to care about what it takes to make the next level up happy  not how you feel, what your career goals are or anything else  you get plugged in where it serves them best.

Pros: Remote work was nice. Although they didn’t pay for office equipment beyond your laptop and docking station. Want a nice chair? Pay for it yourself. Fast internet? Again it comes out of your pocket.
Cons: They didn’t pay for squat.  Even though you may have been working 45 to 60 hours a week for the last three years, you only accumulate the “standard amount”. If you leave the company having took a couple of extra days, they will send you a bill for the difference.  If you are in sales, they will come up with every BS excuse they can not to actually pay you your commission.

Pros: People are very helpful. They almost have to be given the heavy matrix organization.  Telecommuting is a big plus most of the time.  Large company means there's opportunity for growth and movement.
Cons: Working from home is great, but harder to end the work day.  Not always having the opportunity to meet coworkers to develop a good working bond, and understand individual working styles because you either never get to meet them or you might once or twice.  Matrix management  this is a big matrix and not always easy to understand.

Job Title: Principal Datacenter And Cloud Specialty Seller
Pros: Great brand name.  Nothing works better than to have a brand name that everyone knows and a reputation of finishing the work regardless of the price even if they loose money.
Cons: 1st line managers only last about a year so you get a new boss every year.  I had 8 in 7 years.  One boss had me as an employee and we never met each other.  You get the feeling that your not part of a family you are only a number.  They will never pay for training to keep you  qualified for your job.

Pros: The shift from a hardwarecentric to servicecentric and now to a cloud and cognitive service model. A transformation of this kind is not easy for any company with more than 75,000 employees let alone 400,000 that IBM has worldwide. Google reports at 57,000, Apple around than 80,000, Blackberry/RIM at 7000 at its peak to put into perspective.  Blackberry led the market was too comfortable and failed to transform to market demands.   Many, many of the leaders and executives at IBM have Engineering, Computer Science backgrounds  they aren't your typical nowork experience MBAs.  They make decisions very analytically as Engineers tend to do with their clients in mind trying to help solve business and world problems. That problem was once mainframes, servers, storage and systems; evolved to implementing and building IT solutions around that hardware; now it's an hybrid cloud implementyourselfslashbusinessservice.  Very few companies own the entire ecosystem mainframe, business solutions and cloud availability  IBM does. The cognitive guys can request improvements and features to the hardcore engineering server CPU team for maximum optimization making the most advance system easily available to all businesses.    No doubt, IBM is years ahead the competition with their Watson Services and it's built on an ecosystem that is in line with the CIOs and CTOs initiative going into the future.  The platform also lends well to startups and smaller companies being able to leverage and take advantage of IBM's topnotch enterprise and industry services at flexible, scalable and affordable rates.  This is new ground for IBM that was typically reserved for big firms and enterprise companies. Way to go, IBM!
Cons: Old sellers not willing to adapt to what the industry is demanding will have a tough transition. Again, 400,000 employees makes it difficult for any company. People can get comfortable and changing becomes difficult.  Again, Blackberry/RIM is evidence of being the smart phone leader who failed to transform and was just barely saved from a bankruptcy by being acquired for pennies on the dollar. Again, Jim Balsillie, former CEO of Balckberry, had no engineering or computer science background, and tried to run the company solely with his Harvard MBA, which he ran into the ground.  IBM has a lot of work to transform a lot of people who are more comfortable doing things the old way.

Pros: 1. Very professional.  This applied to in terms of approach to tasks, assignment of correct persons to tasks, planning of timelines in respect of resources and workloads and in monitoring of execution.  All around there was a clear understanding of what was involved and what needed to be done.  The work accordingly proceeded smoothly and all knew what slippages were acceptable and which were not. 2. High standards of work.  The quality of work expected was high and it was achieved. 3. Stress free.  There was a refreshing lack of office politics and no undue pressure as all involved had a clear understanding of the processes and what should be done and what could not.
Cons: None experienced during my time at IBM

Pros: For the most part, IBM employees are exceptional; bright, driven, hard working, conscientious, productive.
Cons: In the years that I have been with IBM, it has gone from a company that seemingly valued its employees to a company that only values its bottom line.  IBM no longer provides money for continued education, no longer provides workfromhome employees with necessities such as printers, monitors, keyboards, etc.  Raises are minimal and do not meet cost of living increases.  Bonuses have shrunk over the years to being nearly nonexistent.  Employees work together for years and never meet their fellow department members or managers.  There are several resource actions every year and the employees who remain are expected to pick up the resulting unassigned work load.

Pros: Company values are ethical.  Great salary, health and dental benefits and training. Ability to work from home was much appreciated.  Time off was sufficient.
Cons: Lack of support and communication from their HR.  Overwhelming expectations initially with training and requirements. Need for career better opportunities.  Once contract expired, most jobs were only available for internal candidates.

Pros: IBM is flexible and rewards innovation for those high enough or allowed to introduce it.  Great people work there that want to do good.  Fantastic volunteer programs through "On Demand Community," where one can earn cash rewards for the nonprofit or school they serve with 40 or more hours a year.  Good leadership development programs.
Cons: There is NO loyalty to you or job security.  You can have friends at IBM, but unless you are a very strong performer, NO ONE will stick their neck out for you.  No one.    It's also never a good idea to have opinions contrary to the company line.

Pros: The community of designers is wonderful Solving difficult problems through design Being part of the whole process of design Great place to learn about other design disciplines The organization as a while has come a long way in a few years with regards to incorporating design and design thinking. Still has a long way to go, but there is progress
Cons: Suffers from the typical faults of a large corporation As a visual designer, opportunities to be creative are somewhat limited Overall happiness is VERY dependent on the team and org

Pros: Breadth of learning: so much rich, relevant, timely education at your finger tips  Collaborative environment: colleagues are welcoming and helpful  The sky is the limit on what you can make of your career once you demonstrate your ability to contribute  For a 100+ year old company, the logo and brand are still globally strong, secure, and trusted despite the competition and challenges
Cons: It is obviously a large company, which requires one to be meticulous about focusing on what matters most: clients, collaboration, and making money my words  Overwhelming amount of information, resources, training, materials are available so you have to be extremely diligent to be focused again on what matters most to your role & Client, your manager, and the company.

Pros: Everyone I've met and worked with has been very supportive and cooperative, giving me the support to get up to speed quickly in my position as a newcomer to IBM. I'm loving working with a lot of smart, creative, enthusiastic folks.
Cons: As with all large organizations, there's some momentum hindering agility. For example, one of the tools we use is OK, but there's a newer, more effective one in the market that I'm used to using for my previous employer. It's a bit of a step back to use the 'approved' tool. However, it takes time for IT to review and approve it, and I'm sure they have stricter security requirements than my previous employer, but the organizational momentum is still a bit of a drag with regard to toolsets. Oh, and that's just one example, but there are multiple cases I could name.

Pros: IBM is a stable, wealthy company that has many perks including the benefit package and health insurance avaiable.  IBM employment for the most part is relatively stable.
Cons: IBMers are typically overworked providing services that exeed 40 hours a week including nights and weekends that are just expected.  Balancing personal and work life can be difficult especially since the many positions are work from home.  Additionally, collaboration becomes very difficult in this position since everyone must engage in conference calls.

Pros: Easy onboarding, lot's of self autonomy, strong compensation packages, great benefits, liberal vacation policy
Cons: Too many required conference calls, slim resources through management for training, unrealistic annual goals, too many reorgs and downsizings only to rehire again. Management is aloof and doesn't engage with reports, hard to get internal information, have to rely on the rumor mill. IBM thinks when you walk in the client's door for the first time the sale is 50% over on name recognition. Discontinuing products without fair warning to sales team.

Pros: Telecommuting Flexible  Internal Recorded Training Resources  Lots of mobile tools Has finally recognized need for corporate overhaul of vision Talented resources
Cons: NonUSA staff preferred  Benefits package is below expectations  Severance packages are horrible  Integration teams have little value to incoming staff/companies  Unusual subcontracting practices pro and con Very silo'd corporate environment making it hard to take advantage of a large corporation's resources  Poor execution on new cloud direction  Behind the ball in cloud business  Pay range/bonus not good but reflective of business performance

Pros: IBM has may diverse avenues to travel in any career direction. If one gets tired of their job, they can look within IBM and move to something different within their field of training or something completely different. IBM strives to encourage team work and mentoring, so move to another job can be a good experience.
Cons: There are some areas where IBM has managed to understaff which can cause undue stress. They try to encourage open communication across all levels of management, but sometimes it seems the communication lands on def ears. One has to take the recognition and not stress on the ignored.

Pros: I rejoined IBM because of great people I worked with before that I’d get to work with again. Unsurprisingly I have met even more incredible people who are working sincerely to help our clients and prospects to improve their security posture. Given the long history of patents which reflect the commitment to problem solving through innovation and iteration I’m proud to be a part of that fundamental drive to improve outcomes for people everywhere.
Cons: There’s still some matrixes of complexity that need to be addressed but as the company progresses through transforming to become nimble but firm in its core values I believe these will be addressed.

Pros: I really had a great experience working for IBM. The environment has a lot of trust and collaboration. I was assigned on really great projects even though I was right out of college. There is fantastic flexibility. There is no fixed office time and you can make your own as long as you get your job done. Lots of opportunity to work from home as well. The executives are very down to earth and really rollup their sleeves to work. I may go back to work for the company again after a few years.
Cons: Salary increases are very slow. They make up for it in term of flex benefits, however if you stay here for long, you will lag the market in terms of pay. You may need to then jump a couple of jobs to get back at market pay.

Pros: Everyone is friendly, encouraging, there to help each other grow and learn  ability to work remotely, or work from home flexible and adaptive  professional but not stodgy   successfully turning around their design approach and embracing new methodologies
Cons: as an intern relatively brand new to my field and with all of my team working remotely, I felt at times lost and as though I was missing out on the powerful learning experience of inperson collaboration among my team and other interns of course in fairness to IBM, during the interview process they stressed their desire for someone who was autonomous and took initiative.   Even looking at regular employees, I feel there is a great disadvantage to having teams so spread out but also some advantages, this is certainly an area for IBM to reconsider

Pros: It is a reputed company, and nice to have this brand name on your resume. Salary is competitive if you have other offer. Benefit package is reasonable.
Cons: The work/life balance at IBM is horrible. They want to suck all of your time and energy. IBM literally wants your 24/7 devotion except during your 15 days vacation time. The immediate management always assign tons of work and says you have the flexibility to work from home which they know it is impossible to finish at office. They always fire lots of people and hire fresh graduates. If you argue  little bit with the management you will be on their red list and when the workforce balance time comes which is nowadays almost every year you will  definitely get fired. Salary increment is very poor and you always have to chase the time line. IBM always believe once the employee accepts the job offer, they buy the candidate. IBM is a golden cage where you have no freedom.

Pros: Powerful name in IT. Access to an enormous network of talent. Lots of computer based training available if you utilize it on your own time. Flexible work environment. Access to a broad range of tools and templates sharing industry best practices. Access to experts in just about every IT topic imaginable Nice benefits except for salary
Cons: No loyalty to long term employees You are just a tool in a giant toolbox or a number on a spreadsheet.  You have no meaning beyond that. Low pay compared to industry standards Laughable bonuses and pay raises. No desire or interest in investing in long term employees.  Company would rather replace you than train you in something new.

Pros: Wonderful and bright people.   Reputation is still relatively strong despite decreasing focus on delivering value to clients.  There are still heroic employees to save the day.  Great benefits
Cons: Senior management that focuses only on cost cutting, to the detriment of client satisfaction and employee satisfaction.   Quarterly layoffs.  Decrease in project controls and QA, leading to subpar results for clients.  Reducing US staff and replacing with much less experienced staff in other parts of the world. Fewer and fewer people know what they are doing and how to navigate the IBM structure and processes that continue to change.   17 straight quarters of dropping revenues, and the CEO is not held accountable.

Pros: The people IBMers are great colleagues and people to work. There are plenty of mentors and leaders that can help you to navigate the big corporate world. It offers flexibility with work hours and workfromhome options.  As WW global company, you can travel and see the world. Also, once you in you can explore a lot of different roles without leaving the company.  You can have an opportunity to work on a firstofakind and some research project.
Cons: Birocrarcay. It would be best if you had a lot of approvals to do anything beyond everyday work.  It is a spreadsheet, Wall Street driven company without good care for employees. The previous resource actions were brutal to some groups. Thus, the trust in management is deficient. In many cases, you are just a number on the spreadsheet.  Trust in the brand is becoming iffy.

Pros: Professional development is infinite at IBM with the full spectrum of positions from engineering to business.  Deal with stateoftheart in technology solutions.  One of the few companies which do the entire spectrum in the IT industry from hardware to software, everything can be done inhouse if needed.  Best reasonable respect given to employees regarding worklife balance.  Have to possibilities to explore and find the exact position that interest you.  The employee, including first line managers have excellent people skills.  IBM has its hands in very special markets due to its specialties and legendary status.
Cons: One of the largest companies in the world comes with a large amount of possibilities but with a slow response to feedback.  Compensation is right at industry average levels.

Pros: I was a software development summer intern at the Mass lab in Littleton, MA. The location is really nice during the summer, and the premises feel pretty new. This probably varies for each intern, but the team I was in was really nice and willing to help me with my problems, and we all got along pretty well. Pay depends on the number of credits towards your degree that you've finished, but the rate is relatively good.
Cons: Even as an intern, you can feel the bureaucracy going on in the background. Also, this depends on the team, but be prepared to have a lot of meetings, most if not all of them including having to deal with the joy that is conference calls.

Pros: Strong support for internal and external education. Flexible scheduling. Improved review processes. Support for volunteerism. Great benefits both medical and financial. Positive reinforcement from colleagues is encouraged through BlueThx program. Mentorship encouraged.
Cons: The only downside that I can think of is that change has been slow because of the massive size of the organization. But as the company is turning to an Agile methodology it appears that changes are happening a little more quickly. Also, while IBM encourages employees to learn about new IBM applications, it could do a better job of ensuring that all departments have the means of incorporating appropriate software into their department processes.

Pros: Amazing company  with a culture of innovation, in continuous transformation, leader in AI, Blockchain, and strong position in the battle for the cloud. Salaries are competitive for the industry, there are endless opportunities to grow within the company, nice people, hands off leadership, many more benefits, overall great company to work for.
Cons: continuous change can be challenging for many people to embrace and adapt and then change again change of clients, territories, products on the portfolios, managers, leadership, go to market strategy, new products, new teams ETC = change, change, change, be ready for it. If you can deal with it I personally find it engaging, then you are in good hands

Pros: I enjoy working with really smart people and IBM is filled with them.  People typically have a very wellmeaning, "how can I help" attitude.  The benefits are great with annual rebates for participating in a healthy living program.
Cons: The cash portion of compensation is lacking.  For instance, I've been at the company for four years and have always received "top performer" or "above average contributer" ratings and have received a single 3.5% raise.  Another complaint is the beaurocracy and paperwork required to do anything.  We are significantly less nimble than our competitors because of this.  It can also be difficult for some to work in a matrixed organization where you have to please multiple people, both your direct management and others.

Pros: We'll established systems that work really well.  Expense reimbursements are pretty much clockwork.  Travel agency does a good job.
Cons: Second straight year with 10,000+ layoffs or resource actions as they call it.  Layoffs seemed to be random since some people had 75%+utilization and already booked on projects for most of current year but they were still laid off.  They also had good performance ratings the past few years. Too much self service and hard to get a hold of competent people to help with questions.  Must rely on your own network to get some things done.

Pros: Good benefits and time off, if you can get it.
Cons: No matter what your level of experience is, if you do not brown nose, you will be stuck in the same position until you quit or they fire you. They promote inexperienced managers who are hated because they don't know enough to get out of a locked room. You will be worked to death, and you don't ever expect a thank you. When they decide they want you out, they concoct ridiculous reasons to push you out the door. They lie to clients, don't meet deadlines because their management staff is incompetent and knows zero about the industry. They are behind the times in their thought process, think 1968. Seriously, what other company remotely thinks mainframes are a technological advancement?

Pros: Good benefits Pay is OK but a little below local market average Ability to move around in the company  I've had 3 jobs in 8 years by choice The company has a deep technical stack that is not matched by its competitors
Cons: The market is changing, so is IBM and those changes are painful including lots of job cuts Management changes major focus every few years and abandons thing that were key before they have a chance to produce results Growth by acquisition, not by native development Many customers see the company as having old, outdated technology.

Pros: Liberal vacation, time off ie. sick, funeral, etc Great work from home policy if you work for the right manager/division. No ceiling on your growth potential. Training and learning opportunities abound if you look for them and have the right manger that supports doing that. IBM wants you always learning always growing and always contributing. If you don't like change this is not the place for you. You have to reinvent yourself every 57 years.
Cons: Constant layoffs, horrible middle management. Huge disconnect of local management with corporate Armonk. Pay is different for each region. Find out about the pay for your region first.

Pros: There's only one benefit when working with IBM  work from home.  And that makes it all worthwhile for many.  Unfortunately, they know this, and hold you and your family hostage with low salary, no pay raises, intimidation, long hours, no perks like no internet reimbursement, no cell phone, small cheap workstation etc
Cons: Everything else.  Management has no idea what to do.  There's always a general business direction crises of some sort in play.  Many goal oriented buzzwords appear and disappear without cause, usually daily.  Bluemix, Cloud, Mobile, Analytics etc.  But they all lose support in short time.    You'll be harassed by all levels of management, as it flows from the top down.  You'll be assigned to work some new strategic objective such as Watson, but pulled away when bad numbers are publicized.  You'll be forcibly placed into another invogue area such as Cloud, but that will fail also within a few years where you'll be moved to yet another hotitem such as Agile development.    Sometimes you'll be sent to an entirely different department, perhaps over to customerfacing duties where the customer contract is chaotic and usually in legal contention.  There you'll sit for months doing nothing, except filling out billing forms to keep your utilization numbers up.    From there you'll be pulled from that "account" to another different customer, where the cycle starts again.  Then you'll likely end up back in Mobile or something, where one will languish for a few years until you're finally RA'd – that’s FIRED – not laid off.  Along with 20k others in the US, and 110K world wide.  But wait – Ginny said there’s 20k job openings.  Whew.  Thought it was gonna be a disaster for a second there.  A quick check of the job openings shows a strange removal of jobs after a one week posting.  You’ll print one out and call the hiring manager.    Hiring manager asks where you got the requisition as they are pulled every week.  After you explain, he indicates that there’s a global hiring freeze throughout the company, and his department is no exception.  Feeling compassionate, he explains why he has to post them in the first place, then remove them 7 days later.  And he was never going to be allowed to hire for it in any event.  He’s busy and hangs up.  You'll miss the usual severance, and receive a month's pay before you're escorted to the doors.  You'll also forego your usual 401k match, because they sneakily changed the year's contribution to once/year on December 15th only  and only if you're still with the company on that date.    Then you'll find yourself 57 yrs old trying to find a job with the IBM albatross hanging around your neck.  You'll think back to when you were 30 yrs old, where you were confident and cocky, knowing that nothing like this could EVER happen to you.  You snickered at the old folks, the 55+ crowd, and wondered why in heck IBM didn’t get rid of them so you could get a raise for yourself.  But now at 57, your family and kids will look at you in distain for being unemployed.  You've let them down.  Then you'll come to the realization of why IBM's legal dept is more than 8% of the company when you try to argue age discrimination.  Or why the latest RA took all of your friends over the age of 53, but mysteriously none of the hot shot kids or young management types.  You'll wonder why there's a list of con's of this company that goes on for 20 paragraphs, compared to just 1 for the Pros.  You'll wonder why investors don't see the execs wrecking the place in a hysteria, each taking home $15mil/yr salaries, with $7mil/yr bonuses, and another $45mil/yr in stock options.  You’ll imagine the execs stretched out and sleeping on one of the company’s fleet of 20 large luxury private biz jets on their way to the monthly financial meetings in Europe.  You’ll imagine.  In the meantime, the IRS is after you for some silly 401k malefaction and has put a lien on your house, IBM has sent your name to the credit bureau for a $920.00 trumped up travel voucher you supposedly never paid.  You'll wonder what has happened, or were you just run over by a bus?  Coming home someday you stop by the mailbox and notice a letter from IBM.  It's from Ginny.  She's congratulating you on your "retirement", and offers you a choice of 1 Jelly of the month 2 a jumpstart cable box or 3 a magazine subscription.  I’ll wonder if I should just toss it, or if she’s serious.  She is, and it gets tossed.  As winter sets in, you'll wonder

Pros: Good overall benefits especially the 401k contribution. Methodical and structured approach to business and planning gives some indication of order. The work level can be manageable and overall the work environment is pretty flexible.
Cons: History of moving many high tech positions offshore reduces long term job security in US Frugal to the point of being absurd at times. Pay was decent at first but pay raises were very small. Very bureaucratic. Many levels of approvals and management required to make things happen.

Pros: Ability to work from home
Cons: I worked in IBM Global Services whose only focus was on cost reduction that was done at the expense of their employees and their customers.  Experienced, knowledgeable, highly competent employees were laidoff and replaced with inexperienced resources from other countries.  As a result, productivity and the quality of work produced suffered.  In Global Services, the only thing that mattered was utilization, and it was not unusual to have quarterly utilization targets of 120%130%.  Obviously, in order to meet those targets, especially if you had taken vacation or training time, significant, unpaid, overtime was required on a consistent weekly basis.  Employee raises were very infrequent and small.  Unsurprisingly, morale was very low.

Pros: Great Research Environment.  Great people to work with, and great managers.  The research teams all have toprate researchers, and the managers all seem to know how to run their groups efficiently.  I've never worked anywhere where people meet their software development deadlines like clockwork.  The worklife balance is pretty good there too  I was in to work on a few weekends and I don't think I saw anyone else in the office.
Cons: It may be slightly bureaucratic for silicon valley types used to a startup culture.  Moving up in the company as well as the financial rewards that come with it seems to take time.

Pros: Ability to work from home most days Somewhat flexible at hours, start / stop time Good Technology and resources for job
Cons: Poor poor pay vs other companies Terrible "rating" system No pay for performance No job growth or ability to move to other jobs within IBM

Pros: I love this job, my manager is great and always looking out for his employees.  If he sees an opportunity for advancement, even in another department, that he feels one of his employees is suitable for, he will bring it to their attention and go the extra mile to help them get it.
Cons: Things don't happen fast.  HR is in India so job changes tend to take a long time to complete.  There is also a bit of a Big Brother feel here with all of the security requirements but I guess that's understandable.

Pros: With many any IBM's employees being in the mid 50 year old range, there is going to be many opportunities available for management positions in the upcoming years.  Many people that I work with have worked at IBM their entire career, so there's a TON of knowledge and company history everywhere.
Cons: Too much management; big blue moves slowly because of it. Lot of resistance to change to newer technology, so many of the software tools being used are dated. Not many recent college grads around  lots of older folks. No free lunch or coffee offerings, or any perks for that matter.

Pros: Work with some of the smartest, most motivated people in the world  Exciting work designing, stress testing and implementing world class, enterprise data platform  Learning opportunities are endless,  Great place to learn/grow.   Truly global company  no better place to learn International business
Cons: Need to be comfortable with very fast pace of change needed to drive IBM transformation.  Transformation also requires a lot of "dot connecting"  need to be able to connect disparate information and see unique patterns/issues to deliver best results  not everyone comfortable with being able to do this.

Pros: It has been much better recently with development and management trying to become more agile and using design thinking for the way we work and plan.  No more groups of project managers bugging you for status all the time.
Cons: Although they have gotten better, HR and bureaucracy is a nightmare. I don't want to deal with paperwork and just get back to doing my job.  For a tech company they should be better at automating all our processes.  Also not sure of the current company strategy. It seems all over the place trying to pick out whatever will work.  Going in too many directions at once.  There are way too many VPs that I can't even name.

Job Title: Senior Consultant, Executive Search & Leadership Hiring
Pros: Great culture and teaming; IBMers are very down to earth and pragmatic in approach. Very smart, driven individuals work at IBM, and are willing to help with solving problems and overcoming obstacles.
Cons: IBM is a large organization and learning "who to go to for what" takes time. Not many formal protocols appear to be in place as to how to get work done, so it's often a matter of who you know and connect with to understand the processes. As a plus, this provides an opportunity to work in an ambiguous environment and learn to be nimble and solutionoriented.

Pros: 40% of IBM employees are work from home employees.  They do believe in a work/life balance for the most part.
Cons: The will work you to the bone if you'll let them.  Recently, while the company is making LOTS of money it is not being channelled back in the form of increased salaries or training of their employees.

Pros: For a large company with over 330,000 employees, IBM does many things right as an employer. They pay competitively and have a solid benefits package. They have a great internal training program for things like management and project management. They delegate much of the human resources HR responsibilities to the firstline managers, so that key HR decisions are being made by those with the most knowledge about the employee instead of by HR representatives who couldn't pick the employee out of a lineup. They have a strong mentoring program people who say they don't have a strong mentoring program probably weren't willing to put in the effort and time necessary to make those mentoring relationships fruitful. IBM is large enough that employees can have multiple careers without ever changing companies or having to rollover their 401k.
Cons: Anytime there is a large number of people, communications become harder. Project managers or engineers might think about the number of communication channels, which is nn1/2 where n = number of stakeholders Ref: PMBOK, 3rd ed.. For 330,000 employees, that means IBM has 54.4 billion communication channels. Obviously that is difficult to manage and work within. Recognizing that there is an inherent challenge in the liquidity of knowledge and information can help employees find ways to solve those problems, such as developing wikis for small teams. The other downside to having that many employees means that every time the company spends $3 on each employee, you just spent $1 million. Many employees don't understand this problem, and instead complain about only receiving free ice cream in the cafeteria after project milestone is reached when their cousin at the unprofitable, but well funded, startup is getting free coffee and soda every day.

Pros: Employee benefits healthcare and 401k, competitive salary, work/life balance, promotional ladder, opportunities outside of initial career position, executive management grown internally
Cons: Lower annual bonuses than major consulting companies like McKinsey, Accenture, BCG, etc, rely on "hour glass" resource model so college hires are sometimes isolated from other young professionals in the company if you're stuck on midlong term client site projects.

Pros: There are still advantages, IBM has fully bought into working from home, the groupware and productivity tools are plentiful and useful including mobile and the ability to use Mac products, dogfooding is prevalent so there's ample opportunity to try new products, there's a lot of focus on education.
Cons: IBM stock price continues to decline, and it appears management's solution is to continue aggressive layoffs.  I have worked on 5 different projects in the past two years, each was profitable, but aggressive global resourcing and resource actions led to insufficient and inexperienced support staff, which led to missed SLA's and caused the projects loose profitability.  20% overtime is expected.  IBM appears to be killing off areas of it's business that don't align with the overall vision, even if those areas are profitable.

Pros: I get to work with cutting edge technology on a daily basis. I get to be creative and agile to determine new use cases for artificial intelligence in the real world. Sometimes this is with clients and sometimes this is with internal IBM teams collaborating in order to create the next best use for cognitive.
Cons: Watson can be applied to various industries in many different ways. Goals and metrics are constantly changing so you have to be flexible and motivated to learn new skills to keep up with the fast paced market.

Pros: This is in regards to the IBM business center in Lansing, MI only The work experience is very fast paced and with multiple teams and projects. High profile clients. The benefits are good.
Cons: Lower than the average hiring salary. Very low bonus amounts given annually after a rigorous application process for them. The bonus is so low it only comes out to $20$50 more on your monthly paycheck. No option for title promotion or any bonus given. If you work with all remote clients which the majority of us do the manager of the building still requires you to come in and work. So you waste time in the morning to go to a building where you work with no one and sit in an open office environment to work remotely. Highly distracting and not productive.

Pros: Flexible work from home options. If you are interested in technology and innovation, this is the right place for you. You're asked to constantly change and adapt.
Cons: Constant change sometimes comes without the full solution in place. EPM rollout but missing data to actually use the tools fully in daily work. Bonuses are laughable and employees received such little year end "bonuses" due to IBM lack of performance. Something that most finance employees have very little to do with. Also, such a had drive in finance to pull things forward that we end up playing catchup every quarter to make unrealistic targets...

Pros: Top technology name, great resources for technology smarts.  Large consulting and software business.  Well known name.  Largest global outsourcer.  Recognized worldwide.  Have moved globally quickly with people and sales.  Smarter planet seems to be working well as a marketing campaign.
Cons: Short term focus on people.  Moving jobs overseas at a rapid pace.  Frequent downsizing.  Changes in direction on the consulting side are frequent.   Changes in middle level management frequently.   They have never gotten all the parts of the business working effectively together; often work across purposes.  Losing ground to MSFT and Oracle in enterprise software.

Pros: Decent health insurance if you pay for the stepup plan Well known company Access to all documentation Access to selfpaced training on a variety of topics
Cons: Low salaries in comparison to the market Employees are micromanaged Experienced professionals are treated like children Attendance is taken  Employees might have one square yard of work space in the office Employees are discouraged from working from home, even when their clients request it Long term supplemental employees are not allowed to post for "regular" jobs for 18 months from when they were hired.

Pros: Very smart people, with deep personal and professional commitment, who remain blissfully unaware that they will have no future.
Cons: One of the most depressing, alarmingly arrogant and confused IT companies in the world. Acting like wolves, hunting in small packs, they eventually run out of food and are then forced to eat their own kind.  Greed remains the key motivation for leadership, who will seemingly stop at nothing to best a colleague, weaken a partner or flip a customer. Reckless outsourcing of American jobs for low paid, often unqualified personnel in so called “growth markets”. Stay away from this work environment.

Pros: They have been in business for a very long time, have reinvented themselves repeatedly in order to stay relevant, and they are relevant still. They are also very DEEP and forward thinking in terms of technology, still have one of the cutting edge semiconductor research capabilities along with software as well. No they aren't always as sexy as the latest valley social media knockoff startup but are still, in my mind, as an engineer, pretty solid
Cons: They are a LARGE company, and you do have to spend some time figuring out how to navigate within the organization. Due to their size they can sometimes be. I worry a bit because like many other tech companies, they undervalue doing development domestically at times and are under pressure to streamline in areas where I think in the long term could be leaders

Pros: Benefits as per with IBM employees. Support for benefit is great.  Other than that , I have got nothing.
Cons: Corruption.  When I got selected by client , the recruitment coordinator for IBM contacted me through common friend  small Indian community in CLT to lure me to join to his broinlaw's company which is a vendor to IBM.  When I complained to someone in the  the Partner level , he sent the  recruitment coordinator to India for couple of months  and now , after 2 and half , he is back with the same position same place .  The partner must have got real mad at me for complaining , since after that he never spoke to me and generally everyone in IBM  employees ignores me.

Pros: I joined the Strategic Enterprise Transformation SET team of the Transformation & Operations T&O Organization on April 25, 2017. The SET organizational culture, ways of working, and mission and objectives are the key reasons why I love working at IBM. My current role has given me an opportunity to drive transformation in multiple, creative ways from a stakeholder management and communications perspective. If you're looking for a new and different challenge to redesign the way one of our  most storied global organizations work, please join our team!
Cons: IBM is a very large and complex organization, so it can take some time, patience, and resilience to fully understand how each Business Unit and Function operate to support IBM's performance in the market. Please keep this in mind as you consider opportunities for any role at IBM.

Pros: • Excellent Benefits  • Good Education   • Great Clients and Business Partners  • Great Place to start a career in technology
Cons: • Layoffs quarterly. Experienced, top performing salespeople are being affected.   • Several Sales Managers are not staying educated. They are not leading and/or preparing members of the team to go to the next level. They are not familiar the team’s job tasks. Focused on playing politics with other managers.  • The “Bonus Plan” is too subjective. Sales reps on this plan are paid from a pool of money. Managers determine how much each sales rep makes.  • Limited career growth

Pros: You get to work with intelligent people who are also nice.  Brandname recognition.  Generous compensation package.  Being able to telecommute saves time wasted sitting in traffic, helps the environments, and boosts employee productivity.  I'm not a morning person, but happily works late into night sometimes if needed.  Management in general are competent and understanding.  It doesn't hurt that employees get all sorts of little perks, too, from discount show/movie tickets to free museum admission, from travel priviledges cheaper car rental, hotel stays to employee pricing at some of the customer websites  Apple, Sony, Panasonic, GE, Sharp, Philips, to name a few.
Cons: Politics, politics, politics.  A lot of decisions are made from top down.  Bureaucracy.

Pros: work from home mobility is nice.  IBM has nice logo items.
Cons: Senior management is only interested in keeping stock price high.  IBM is always offshoring jobs.  2/3 of IBM employees are outside the US now.  Vacation blackout dates for a total of 2 months each year.  Management has not mentioned a word to it's US employees, and over 5,000 have lost their jobs in the last two weeks.  They rule by fear and intimidation.  When you manage good business results, you don't get a raise, and instead are fed the line "at least you have a job" all while IBM records record revenue.

Pros: Reasonably good people work at IBM
Cons: Everybody's hands are tied.  Nobody can help you.  You will be paid as little as possible while your benefits are chipped away.    There is a strong sinking ship feeling.  Early this year there was a significant layoff.  Just a few weeks ago, furlough.  This is scary.

Pros: In the fifteen years I was there, I worked with many very talented people across the globe.  In the late '90's, talent and technical depth were developed, nurtured and expected to excel, and work/life balance and the internal culture was built to retain the best of the best.  The people within IBM from that period, in the first two management tiers, are outstanding.
Cons: With the Service Delivery Center concept, people became commodities, and the brain trust in services was drained.  Work life balance eroded along with benefits, training and retention.  Executive direction became obsessed with quarterly reporting to Wall Street and the bonuses at the expense of long term performance planning and responsible expense planning, resulting in whimsical and contradictory leadership.

Pros: Work life balance is great. More than average flexibility to work from home whenever needed. Several teams only work in office twice a week.
Cons: Management is still operating under the former company, good Ole boy system. If you're not white and or a male, you don't stand a chance of promotion, unless your manager/ement is from the traditional IBM. Otherwise, all of HIS people will get the promotions and or pay increases.

Pros: IBM is learning from past mistakes. They are continuing to improve in areas that matter to employees. If you are a top contributor your pay scale and rewards are fantastic. Unlimited opportunity to learn in all areas of any IT business Brand recognition opens opportunities for future career changes however IBM is so large you have potential to do anything you like and they actually offer the checkpoint to get there.
Cons: IBM is a very large company so processes and change take time.  Even though there is an improvement in transparency from executives it still seems like there is a lot to improve. IBM is changing business in the right direction however previous mistakes still haunt and the "front line" is still paying for those mistakes via retention or lack of ability to replace skilled workers.

Pros: Opportunity to work with and learn from leaders in your field.   Access to highend computing resources leaders in quantum computing   Company has high visibility. Opportunity to make a large impact   Opportunity for remote work, flexible with work hours and days off.   High Morale
