Pros: The work/life balance especially for a systems engineer is amazing. There are times when things are hot and when they are pretty cool. In all, I will rank them high in this area.  In my experience, I had access to all kinds of learning resources. Self development is a big deal it appears. I had access to all kinds of materials from text books, to articles, to lectures, etc through the IBM learning portal. Oh boy did i milk that thing!  I had the opportunity of working various kinds of projects which also helped so much in my professional development.   I had the opportunity of trying out new devops application and practices because there is preponderance of hardware resources that enabled me to do this. Mind you, this may not be the case for everybody. My position systems engineer, gave me access to a lot of compute resources and placed me at the frontline of problems.  The company also paid for all my education expenses that saw me obtain my master degree I don't know if they still do this  A lot of solid, old technology talents  They may have problems with doing things the new way though I mean driving Infrastructure as code, self healing automation etc
Cons: The chain of commands can make it difficult to innovate. I had to push and pull to drive change more importantly though, your direct manager is very important here. My manager was not the best at advocating for her workers.  The pay can also be very low I got a little over double the amount I made while in IBM as an advisory Engineer when I transitioned to another company. For the last three years of my total 8, I was without pay raise.  They are also beginning to go in the direction of other 'woke' corporate cultures across the US by driving "diversity and inclusion" to its insane end. They have adopted the CRT training in their learning modules basically attempting to brainwash members of staff along the 'woke' thoughtprocess.  The performance criteria and measurement are very nebulous and quite difficult to navigate for me, your experience may be different.

Pros: Team of professionals, lots of opportunities to learn and advance your career, typical business hours, but workload is heavy.
Cons: Need more people on teams to help with heavy workload. My department kept me from moving upwards because they couldn’t afford to lose me due to the heavy workload and time to train new recruits. Put in lots of OT and I was salaried. No work/life balance.

Pros: Working for IBM you get to be a part of technologies and processes that are changing the world. The free educational opportunities they offer to all of their employees is world class.
Cons: There is sometimes restructuring that can be painful and change the dynamics of your teams, but I believe most of those pain points are behind us as we transitions to a new kind of IBM.

Pros: IBM doesnt believe in micro management of employees instead trust them to be self motivated to bring meaningful outcome/excellence in job. There is enough of space given to create room to bring in new thoughts/idea which matter most to IBM and its Client. Each employee is kind of partner in IBM. Great work culture.
Cons: IBM is not a good pay master, very process oriented, many times your progression get stuck in process and you could be victim of it. you have to really smart to find ways.

Pros: The people, the people, the people.
Cons: The hours, the short term view and short sightedness of senior management.  The need to run the business to please Wall Street and boost the stock price despite the fact that Wall Street has not proven itself of late to be a bastion of insight.

Pros: It is a good opportunity to see the next generation of IBM offerings and their performance.  The engineering staff tends to be absolutely ingenious.
Cons: The work flow management tends to be erratic because the priorities are not well defined.  This leads to having the staff feel like no progress is being made to complete any goal.

Pros: Large company, good pay, good resources and benefits
Cons: I often think IBM only survives because of its name. We lost a lot of business to Accenture and Deloitte and the management of people on the bench is not great. While my manager had more consulting experience, she was not a SME in org change. Her feedback was useless.

Pros: First, let me say that with a company size as large as IBM it's nearly impossible to get a glimpse understanding of the organization as a whole, since it's so big and covers so many different avenues. This review is specifically for that of their services organization formally aka ITD, now GTS.  The company is striving to make efforts to insource jobs within the U.S. by opening up "delivery centers" and dismantling the 'workathome' concept. By encouraging collaboration, and utilizing other resources with various backgrounds and expertise, the plan is to "support" as many clients as possible, while providing it at a reasonable price, and still making a profit.  Great Resume Builder Learn a lot about processes, procedures, audits, internal  work within the Organization that you can bring to another organization It's IBM chances are, not many have seen what you have seen and can bring to the table eg. Variety of clients, industries, infrastructures, challenges IBM is still a great company that does many great things, and at times you'll work with some very great people, but the talent pool is declining greatly
Cons: This organization has improved from years prior, however it's growth is stagnant at times, and it's vision is unclear. The problem with this methodology is that there are some who are over utilize way over capacity, doing the work of 3 FTE, while other's can sit on their rearends and support a very nonbusy client.  The pay is far below average compare to the industry average, promotions and growth are nonexistent, and IBM is losing it's quality brandname by hiring many 'unqualified' very limited skilled employees both outside and inside the country.  Very Stressful at times Continuous cuts and restrictions of OT  No growth Below average pay  Losing Brand Image low skill employees with nothing more than high school diplomas

Pros: The younger new hires are generally very bright and dedicated and truly want to excel to the best of their abilities and ambitions. A good opportunity for new grads to get good initial experience and skills up to speed. The fact that nearly everyone in the US works from home is a time and money saver and frees you up to live wherever you like.
Cons: It's a company run by lawyers and accountants not software or technical people or even IT people. Pathological levels of micro micro micro management and 'metrics'.  The process by which you have to do something is more important that doing something.  No increases or promotions, ever. Not ever. Whatever you are hired at, that's it. Get used to it. No money for training even if it's local and forget about travel to training or professional and peer conferences. There is no upper limit on bureaucratic paperwork and people you have to go to get the least thing done.

Pros: Fair salary, good health care benefits. A CEO that has a solid vision for the future of the company.
Cons: Bureaucracy. Long time managers and long time employees refuse to change. Travel freeze and expense cuts. No pay raise in more than two years. Perception that the company is cheap and in financial trouble. No stability and constant fear of layoffs.

Pros: Enjoyed the remote office environment and easy hours.
Cons: Execs over sell, Managers over commit, PMs underestimate and you are left on an ever shrinking team because of layoffs & attrition to deliver a solution to a customer that is already upset by the time you get to them because of all of the fumbles and additional charges that have occurred, that once they find out that they will receive the most basic of implementations by way of licensing tiers on everything they need thus ending up with something similar to a "small office" type configuration for their company by way of licensing.

Pros: Prestigious name recognition for the average person Company protects the "brand name" at all costs. Dividend checks are nice but at what cost Low wages, layoffs, business unit selloff, stagnant innovation
Cons: Internal turmoil, unhappy customers, disgruntled employees, jobscared work environment.  Many layoffs have occurred and the layoffs will only continue.  It is inevitable. Business unit selloffs and closings .  Current company leadership is clueless regarding how to "right the ship".

Pros: IBM is great to work for. It offers many opportunities which can sometimes be overwhelming and thus it is great to have a good boss who will support you during the steps. Tou are encouraged to exceed and participate in as many opportunities you can grasp, as long as you keep a high performance score.
Cons: Your bosses, as it is a matrix management, can be all over the place globally, so lots of conference calls can include calls outside of your working hours.

Pros: Global company with lots of opportunities to work on global assignments.  Great company to have on your resume
Cons: Upper management has shared several times that the only reason we are located in the U.S. is because the client mandated it. They would send this work offshore if they could. Doesn't make you feel valued as an employee.   they don't pay for the amount of work we have

Pros: Endtoend job, where you work with people all over the world and have stimulating, challenging work,  working with new products and needing to be flexible and ready to do whatever it takes to get the job done.    Duties start with gathering requirements, writing technical requirements, working with developers to produce,, test and implement business intelligence software.  Afterwords, working with client to resolve and smooth out any problems or tweaks needed.  Later,  working on production problems as they occur. and working on new requirements once in steady state.  Environment is complex and you have to be able to learn quickly how to find your way around.  There is data warehouse, business intelligence, data mining, data visualization, etc.  Work is reporting and analysis for various help desk environments such as ISM, ServiceNow, Remedy and others.  Also on occasion doing training and demos and mentoring new hires.  Working remotely is also plus in that you do not have travel time and can concentrate on getting the job done.  Also within limits hours are pretty flexible.
Cons: Trend is to offshore as much work as possible, so both regular and contract employees are eventually facing layoffs.  Regular employees typically work long hours while contract employees have reduced hours for several periods during the year.  Also, contract employee paid tends to be low when compared to the market average.

Pros: It is a good company with a lot of accounts clients across all industries, which means that invariably, an IBM India practitioner spends a lesser time on the bench. The GBS accounts follow some of the widely accepted and rigidly followed standards for quality delivery.
Cons: A highly process oriented company, which lags behind when it comes to employee benefits and rewards. The perks and compensation are low and way below market rates.

Pros: Culture is really coming along at IBM. Parts of the company have done a lot to advance towards current trends. There has been solid flexibility during the pandemic, and tons of support.
Cons: Like all giant corporations, change is slow. Leadership often feels the need to validate their existence by micromanaging. That is slowly going by the wayside, but patience is a must if you seek to make a worthwhile career at IBM.

Pros: Some of the most brilliant minds in the world have passed through IBM's doors. The opportunity to find them and work with them is presented daily
Cons: The brightest minds of our world... move to where they are rewarded for taking concepts and turning them into reality and not just hyped research to be sold by patent lawyers.

Pros: You will work with one many of the brightest, motivated, creative and loyal people that you will meet in your life. They offer a very complete benefits package. Many opportunities to work from home if that's important to you.
Cons: The large size presents many issues.  The current matrix management model makes it difficult, if not impossible, to serve all managers. Most managers are responsible for large teams and frequently have lost touch with employees and work loads. Regardless of your contribution, be prepared to be evaluated to a matrix. IBM doesn't develop their employees.

Pros: The team was full of very smart very talented developers and testers. The location was convenient for many people. Farmer's market was across the street
Cons: Micromanaging became extremely overbearing.  All requirements started to become unreachable, more content was expected in less time.  As employees began leaving one at a time, the requirements stayed the same, requiring many hours of unpaid overtime

Pros: Smart people but they can't get out of their own way.  Everything is decision by group.  No one can make a decision.  Great work/life balance because there are a hundred people doing the same jobyou can hide, and many do, in the ranks of IBM.
Cons: IBM has different pay scales for men and women.  I know because my colleagueseach with less experience than me made over 50k more than me for the same job, lower performance.  The company drives mediocrity in everything.  The managers have been around forever and have a good ol' boy mentality.

Pros: The customers do appreciate the extra effort you put into helping them.  Some of my customers and colleagues have turned into lifelong friends.
Cons: Myself and several other US located colleagues on our team got their jobs moved to either Ottawa, Canada or Eastern Europe.  This was done to save IBM even more money, not due to lack of profitability in our department.  One Third of IBM employees are in India or Bangladesh.  This isn't an accident.

Pros: IBM offers great flexibility both in terms of work schedule and position. They help you find what works for you.
Cons: It can easy to fall through the cracks if you are not proactive. Some tools and workflows are pretty outdated. Also, there was quite a long hiring gap, which means there are basically two cohorts of engineers and it can be hard to bridge that gap in terms of experience.

Pros: IBM recently updated its parental leave policy, expanding the program considerably for birth mothers, fathers, partners and adoptive parents and it made me feel very appreciated as a working parent. Moms in particular, can now take up to 20weeks paid leave, which is life changing.  IBM also promotes a very flexible working approach. There is a great deal of trust for you to work autonomously.
Cons: Like any big company, there are many layers of approval, which can impact the progress of a project.

Pros: My immediate Engineering and Development team were great to work with. Worklifebalance is great as well as the ability to workfromhome. Performance is rewarded generously with great Benefits. The opportunity for growth is tremendous, but you have to keep up with technology trends and the vision of the company in order to be part of the leading edge.
Cons: Executive Management can be cutthroat with eliminating teams and positions. Make sure the project you are working on is in line with the company's future vision in order to maintain your employment.

Pros: High level of expertise, dedication, sharing, diversity, brings actual inclusion of each and every team member, presentably, to a new level. Opportunities to contribute, build the next gen infra for clients, and make a diff are endless.
Cons: Hard to shine among this level of expertise!

Pros: Big Blue has freshly reinvented itself as the leader in hybrid cloud and AI technology. There are astonishing strides being made in research and product development, and we need all the talent we can get our hands on. Development, design, marketing: whatever your skills are, we need them.
Cons: This is a giant organization and everyone, including/especially management, has a lot on their plates. Be prepared to be self directed.

Pros: Some very intelligent coworkers...when you can find them Large resources and thought leadership...if you know how to navigate the org Good work like balance
Cons: Too many hands in deals...people get paid when the don't contribute They don't pay enough in Client Executive roles If you are not a lifer, your chances of coming in and moving up are limited

Pros: Diverse learning environment. Great for entry level techs needing to get lots of hands on time.
Cons: Lots of work, with little staff to cover all the work. You are asked/expected to do 6080 hours of work in a 40 hour week. No OT, any work over 40 hours is required to be "Flexed" out. Employees are severely underpaid!

Pros: It was a great place to work and grown.  I gamed lots of experience and got to meet very nice people.  I loved the new challenges that came with the territory. I was never board because they was always new things to learn all the time.
Cons: They laid off when times get hard instead of reducing the entire team time and hours.

Pros: I was on the road constantly and often was living outside the US  which for me was a great way to see the world
Cons: Most of the work that was done was focusing on selling their software, not really focusing on the strategic issues.  I was often told to lie to clients about the amount and type of experience I had to get on projects as IBM's priority is to maximize revenue and they do so by pitching staff at a higher level than they actually are.

Pros: Benefits, plenty of opportunities for those willing to travel, many positions can be performed at home.  Good place to get experience at the beginning of one's career, plus working for IBM looks great on a resume.
Cons: Most of the money, bonuses, and opportunities go to people in specific areas those that IBM is focusing on at a given moment.  Currently that would be big data, cloud, mobile, etc.

Pros: The Ability to work from home.  Some flexible hours.  No accrued sick time needed, when you are ill you simply take the time to get well again as you are not limited to a certain amount of days.
Cons: The last few years have brought longer hours, more stress, flat wages, no upward mobility, no training, loss of pension, the 401k bilk, worsening health care coverage, loss of fellow FTE's with ever increasing cheap foreign labor and abused contractors who have regular furloughs

Pros: Unlimited resources. Executive technical career path with profit sharing for nonmanagers. World leader in R&D. Very good open door policy with high respect for the individual. Surrounded by bright, energetic people. Nonconfrontational work environment. Compensation and benefits on par with the industry.
Cons: Worklife integration policy can cause work to have priority over family life if not carefully managed. The company is redefining itself, reducing workforce and selling off business units, i.e. PC Company and x86 Server business.

Pros: Access to educational materials to grow skill set.  People who are genuinely interested in seeing the company thrive.  Kind of hard to come up with more pros; many of them are no longer pros.
Cons: One size fits all work location policy toward a global company of 400K employees is not the most wise approach.

Pros: IBMers around the world share a strong commitment to each other and the success of our clients  Great place to work, highly collaborative environment  Opportunity to engage in technology and capabilities that will change the world  Operate at a global scale, but working together in small agile teams
Cons: Pace of change in technology and our industry is accelerating, so requires our company and our employees to constantly reinvent

Pros: I love the benefits and the work/life balance.  I can work from home and create my own schedule.  My work is important and rewarding
Cons: While IBM communicates a lot, the important things are often not communicated.  When my last 2 supervisors left, I didn't find out until the day before they left.  New people are brought in without an explanation about their role or what they will be doing.  Career growth can be challenging

Pros: Good benefits, flexible work schedule, up to date online learning, pleasent work atmosphere.
Cons: Pay is below market  difficulty moving forward in career  management puts you where it is most beneficial to them and makes it difficult to approval any career moves. Layoffs tend to occur on a yearly basis. Work week is 40+ hours  if you’re hourly you tend to receive no OT but are told to balance hours  take time off

Pros: Thought it was a great company to work for, but through the years it has gone down hill and not only that, most everything is going to China. Is this the sign of a good company? I will never buy anything IBM because I am boycotting China. I bet Watson is rolling in his grave. He believed his employees came first. Current CEO say employee's are th.
Cons: Same as above. I should have put cons here, but couldn't find any pros at this point.

Pros: They really are walking the talk when it comes to how best to provide feedback in a fastmoving, social environment. While the outside debate rages on about the value of performance management systems, IBM has done something about it, and has spent time listening to em…
Cons: We'll wait to see how well managers can incorporate this. Any performance review and coaching system is only as good as the managers who implement it. But the basics are all there for them to use.

Pros: excellent benefits. opportunities for advancement , publications and patent applications to advertise your engineering know how and expertise. network with the most advanced people in the world
Cons: the benefits and perks can be be viewed as good from one perspective, but the other side of the coin is that it can be considered waste that could otherwise be used to create more profit for shareholders or salary for employees

Pros: Where it matters, this company has a seat at the table  with industry, with government, with decision makers who are setting the agenda for public private partnerships.
Cons: Easy to get sucked into long days, projects and work because there is a lot to learn with a fast changing industry and so many important new tech spaces where the company wants to lead.   Also the pace of change here is relentless, it defines this industry and us to stay one step ahead in service of clients.

Pros: Continuous learning while advancing your career and supportive management.
Cons: Challenging misconceptions of IBM's lack of market relevance.

Pros: Pay was great. Schedule was perfect for me. Was very successful and praised by the user base in my building, but that is because I took the initiative to solve problems and update KB for others. Our Anthem Supervisor was awesome!
Cons: Very little training or support once IBM took over for Anthem. Trying to submit timecards and apply for PTO was an absolute nightmare using Lotus notes. Upper management for IBM changed the culture and that is when I left.

Pros: Company values, options to develop, people are great, many opportunities to explore new roles
Cons: Individual career navigation is purely who you know, upward mobility can be halted, pay transparency is not as open as it should be, big company = bureaucratic issues

Pros: Flexibility in working hours, Mobility
Cons: Zero concern for morale you should be thankful you have a job here, grossly underpaid, unrealistic expectations for amount of work that one person can do.

Pros: Great brand. Impressive consistency for a 100 year old company, nice people.
Cons: Too many layers of management, below average sellers, multiple sales overlays for every software group, cap earnings for sales, poor execution with technology delivery teams. Sadly, IBM isn't where top performers go to work, it's where they go to retire.

Pros: Challenging Work environment  Plenty of Opportunities to Learn Lean Manufacturing is taught to all interested New work every day
Cons: Little Care for Work  Life Balance Lean manufacturing is taught, but not well implemented / managed Upward Mobility chances are limited Salary Plan and Career Development are not managed well

Pros: There was always plenty to do and learn.  My coworkers were friendly.
Cons: There was too much work, little training on the actual tasks, general lack of management my manager had no actual managerial experience, didn't know the subject area of the employees he supported.  Very stressfilled.  Required to work day and night, sometimes 1416 straight hours, then take off at the end of the week instead of getting paid OT.

Pros: Good pay and plenty of exposure to training and opportunity to use training and good pay for overtime effort.
Cons: When Mainframes were being replaced by Pcs and Pc networks IBM wanted to decrease my salary by $10 fro $25 per hour to $15 per hour and little or not opportunity for overtime and I had an obligation for child support for 3 children to my exwife, so I had to leave IBM and get a job with a medical company as a field engineer on a Medical CAT Scanning equipment.

Job Title: Senior Software Engineer, And Systems Development Manager Prior
Pros: excellent technology company with a recognized brand worldwide. A career where there is endless technology job possibilities for qualified staff. Contact made throughout the IT industry.
Cons: IBM is a place that is not for everyone. IBM allows you freedom to fail and freedom to succeed. The choice is yours but be ready when you first start to wear the eight stripe logo

Pros: Excellent people and products. Talented SME's and specialists in every area of IT. Wide range of products.
Cons: Unbelievably complex and incoherent management process. Lots of empty suits. Low morale with ongoing layoffs of talented and experienced people. The company is slow to react  to customers and industry. Many software products are too complex to be useful to anyone but the most sophisticated enterprises.

Pros: Fosters innovation with a focus on patenting,  research, and development.  Highly profitable.  Focuses on education of employees for the betterment of the company.
Cons: So profit driven that it can’t compete with Amazon which rewards employees and channels all cash flow back into the business which drives the stock and attracts talent.

Pros: The people you work with are the best people in the world.  The smartest you'll ever meet.
Cons: The so called leadership is terrible.  Everyone above your first line manager is disconnected, uncaring, bureaucratic, out for themselves, and clueless.   Arbitrary firings of people based on made up performance measurements.    New health insurance plans for 2019 do not provide an option for out of network coverage.

Pros: The teams, processes, professionalism, salary, benefits ...
Cons: Some executives are too focused on unnecessary goals and totally unrealistic numbers  so projects become about numbers rather than serving the customer. Also, IBM has lost MANY top performers due to the unnecessary focus to bring every employee into an office. Many of the best resources are gone due to forced relocation requirements.

Pros: good culture,growth,good infrastructure,good people It holds up better in recessions: We may be in a bull market now, but these don’t last forever. Once the rally ends, most stocks will drop. But some will fall harder than others.
Cons: Stagnant Revenue Growth,Declining EarningStagnant revenue has led to declining earnings at IBM. IBM’s net income fell 4.45% yearoveryear in the most recent quarter, the third quarter of 2017.  IBM’s net income over the trailing 12 months, $11.31 billion, is less than its net income in 2016 $11.87 billion. In 2015, IBM earned $13.19 billion.

Pros: IBM provides an innovative, collaborative work environment where you can build the career you want. I have always had excellent managers who wanted me to succeed and cleared the path. The compensation is excellent.
Cons: IBM can be kind of a battleship. It is not as nimble as a startup and sometimes it feels we are always trying to boil the ocean and do everything rather than a few things well. That can be frustrating.

Pros: Learning and career opportunities, flexible working hours, home office availability
Cons: Worklife balance in the back office functions is extremely difficult to be maintained at senior level. The senior subject matter experts have to cope with the high workload driven by the complexity and the speed of changes in the business while being hindered by the poor competency of the colleagues who are supposed to provide support.

Pros: Overall IBM is a great company to work with.  If you are willing to stay up to date on technology and are willing to grow its def the place to be.  But if you just want to be a geeky computer nerd and want to code all day then IBM is not for you!  IBM is meant to take the computer nerd and turn him or her into a leader.  Yes, IBM is hiring many people offshore, and yes half of them are idiots, but guess what?  Look at the people that are leading them?  Folks from the US!  Listen, anyway one can code, but not everyone can be a leader, and IBM is a great company in which can turn you into a leader.  That's only if you want to be a leader!
Cons: Work/Home life is not the greatest.  As a IBM employee I have given up holidays, weekends and family special events due to work.  I literally work a minimum of 12 hours a day "on a good day", but I am told I can only bill 40 hours a week.  Second bad thing with IBM is that, if I'm going to work so much and sacrifice my family, and personal time I should be compensated with a fair salary.  I mean lets really be honest, show me 1 project in which a consultant worked 40 hours a week.  Don't get me wrong I have obtained excellence awards and bonuses, but nothing beats a overall good salary.

Pros: good to get a couple of years exeprience but after that move on.
Cons: IBM is foucsed on cost cutting and unless you have a much needed specialty they are not interested in career employees in US since they can pay global resources much less.   They even hire contractors in other countries to keep cost down.   So should be viewed as short term employment

Pros: Get to work on some interesting ASIC hardware design projects
Cons: High stress, 7 day work weeks expected, high overtime expected, expected to work while on vacation.

Pros: You have the ability to work with people all around the world and learn so much.  You will have access to test and try all of the cutting edge technology.
Cons: You have to manage your career.  I found managers who are willing to help.  However with IBM going mostly mobile in the US.  It is hard to keep up these relationships.  Being part of a global team was fun but still need to have the office experience.

Pros: The company actually invested in their employees: provided tools, decent laptop and phone, and sent away for actual dedicated training in a classroom setting not just DVD or online material to be accessed during slow periods or free time.
Cons: No real way to work/get out from under bad/poor manager or their decisions; inevitably suffer the demise of unfortunate assignment.

Pros: Big, Many Customers who still think "No one got fired for buying IBM" That is changing are still providing forward motion, but with quickly decelerating momentum.
Cons: Big, Too Late to Too Many Things.  Slow moving, Top Down oriented model, with seeming seriously lacking leadership at numerous levels.  Atmosphere of fear, and back stabbing of long time high achievers.  Killing their best by finger pointing, and blaming everyone but high level leadership.

Pros: Great technology, smart product managers, good communications and knowledge development
Cons: HIghly political in places where here is little oversight due to high level of contractors  perhaps. Many managers seem more interested in impressing each other than developing good processes and delierables because they actually care about quality.

Pros: Good Benefits and working arrangements. Salaries not in the top tier but adequate.Lateral movement is expected as is "volunteering" for more work outside your particular silo.
Cons: Huge company that apparently trains management not to listen.  The age 50 barrier is alive and well though not provable due to the archaic bell curve performance rating / pay scale system. Raises are nonexistent

Pros: Exposure to wide array of industries and good work life balance compared to other consulting firms Heavy investment in talent from time as a consulting intern to graduateentry consultant to senior consultancy Domestic and international projects alike Plenty of room for growth in the CbD program and opportunity to lead or make a difference Both strategic and implementation projects in portfolio
Cons: Big company and therefore difficult to get a hold of certain resources if not planned for Skill sets are needed for particular roles

Pros: Big company=lots of diverse opportunities. Company embraces work from home as applicable while encouraging direct interpersonal interactions with clients and team members.
Cons: Today's workforce wants more immediate recognition and advancement. While ibm does accelerate promotion cycles, it does still take time to gain exposure to all of the diverse assignments one might desire, and need to show their capabilities.

Pros: They know and understand good companies with good people/products/services to acquire.  I have met some really hard working brilliant good people at ibm.
Cons: Terrible internal processes.  Still on lotus notes!!  Admin doubled after being acquired by IBM.  Homegrown systems that do not talk to one another.  Embarrassing to defend inefficiencies to clients.  Answer to declining revenue is to get rid of good people, remove option to work from home and add more administration.  Have lost really good team members to bad management decisions.

Pros: Can work from home.  Good health benefits.
Cons: Little to no training on IBM unique systems/process. Antiquated back office so quotes take a long time.  Below industry comp.  Constant turnover & cutting cost.

Pros: Work with hybrid cloud technology. Teammates have deep skills. Our team works well together.
Cons: Challenging year because of the pandemic. Working remotely can make you feel somewhat isolated. I miss being able to do design work in person with everyone in the same room.

Pros: You get to work with a lot of really smart people and have access to a lot of training. They want you to do at least 40 hours of training a year.
Cons: Don't count on retiring from IBM. IBM prefers young, cheap, and inexperienced. They don't care how much training you have done or how well you perform. One moment you're vital for their future success and the next moment you're gone.

Pros: They have several different departments that encompass almost every facet of Information technology so its a good place to learn and expand your skillset. They also provide a fun environment to work in. They have a huge complex with a restaurant and a gym inside and some of the managers are really nice.
Cons: Its difficult to move up in the ranks because its an old company. Also there are some racial issues at the plant in Boulder. Big problems that cant be resolved easily or through through political rhetoric.

Pros: Good work environment. Challenges resource reskilling at the highest level, Allows you to be yourself or be inclusive while working. Allows your voice to be heard through company surveys.
Cons: Learning how to cope with stress and certain working conditions where timelines are involved.

Pros: In the technical field, innovation is always happening, in many areas all at the same time. Learning becomes critical to be able to connect various technologies that are growing, but are different. But will be even better when utilized together. That's what learning helps me to do. IBM encourages me and provides a platform for me to indulge my learning appetite.
Cons: I would like to see more learning styles, like in the "TED Talk" format.

Pros: Love working at IBM. We do meaningful work that runs the world economy. Management is great, and expectations of employees is appropriate.
Cons: Facilities are 30years outdated with little sign of site investment. Pay scale appears to be a bit below the market average, so you have to love what you do here, otherwise you will likely find employers offering more money for a similar position.

Pros: Largely work from home. Pay is fair but not outlandish. The benefits are fair but not outlandish—very stable and good place to spend a career. IBM values technical skills and sales skills. IBM is a good company.
Cons: A big company, and sometimes people get caught in the crossfire when IBM decides to redefine itself. Not a place to get super rich. Lots of bureaucratic red tape, and hard to get stuff done.

Pros: If you enjoy working within the realm of complete chaos, this job's for you.  If you look forward to working 60+ hours a week, with little to NO guarantee that you'll reap ANY reward, this job's for you.  The single, shining positive is the wonderful people that have managed to survive the wrath of Sammie.
Cons: Complete lack of respect for the individual  You're treated as a component rather than a living, human being.  You simply can NOT trust anyone at the executive level

Pros: Large company opportunities to branch off in varying careers.  Many locations that also allow for mobility to move near or away from love ones.  Software and service driven company so the sale of commodities is not included as part of the company structure.   Only enterprise and Medium / Small business services and products are extended
Cons: The promotion system if very subjective.  Great talkers but poor workers get frequent recognition.

Pros: I've had success with pay as a contractor, the experience is really good and the company name on your resume is great.
Cons: Work/life balance is certainly swayed toward work. IBM's "lean" service model leaves much to be desired, we constantly run undermanned and the customers would be much happier with dedicated people as compared to a team of people who can work on any customer account.

Pros: Aggressive software acquisition strategy. Ability to work from home.  A great place to start ones career and build a foundation of skills.
Cons: Subjective performance reviews.  Monthly driven quota objectives versus quarterly.  Too few reps make their quota objectives with quota assignment tied back to Wall Street expectations versus reality.  Too many layers of top management who add little value.   IBM is supposed to be "family friendly"  but taking vacation days is not encouraged.

Pros: I only worked for IBM for 18 months and was then laid off. However during that time I found them open and honest with employees and customers alike. I would not hesitate to work for them again. the work was exciting and you never stopped learning.
Cons: So big they tend to trip over their own feet at times

Pros: The company provides decent health benefits, flexible working hours, and the ability to move into different job roles during the course of your career. There are so many jobs at IBM that it is  not that hard to get hired.   However, there are many problems at IBM.  there are more cons than pros.
Cons: Read Robert Cringely's book.  It is all true.

Pros: The amount of paid time off you are entitled to,  the ability to work from home,  employee benefits and discounts and  the coworkers.
Cons: each quarter there are numerous lay offs and after putting in 10+ years people are only given 4 weeks severance pay

Pros: vast technology, concepts and people with desire to do good.
Cons: IBM been broken long time. $100B to 80B in 4 years, hampered by lack of leadership, risk averse most managers managing up for their jobs. Vision not clear and lack of communication down the ranks. have to find out 3rd party how and what IBM is doing, Lack of career direction

Pros: Trainings provided on tools/new things, my management group is very fostering of my happiness, never stressed out, flexible work from home whenever and not strict 95pm, opportunity for travel to other US citiesall expensed, room for growth, topnotch benefits, healthy stocked kitchen, etc
Cons: Some boring days there is not much work at all since it's such a big companyvery typical, not that many company outings, some departments very separated from my group

Pros: IBM is transforming itself and I think we are about to change the world with our Watson technology. IBM challenges you every day. The benefits are quite good as well.
Cons: They moving away from the mobile employee program and requiring employees to commute into offices again. It is a challenge if you do not live near one. Seem to be interested in younger, new hires and eliminating employees that have been at the company for 10 or more years.

Pros: Flexible hours.  Relaxed dresscode.
Cons: Used to have more flexibility as to where you worked; that's going away.  Salary / Bonuses  falling behind. Company is being managed to maintain profit margin while revenues have declined for 5+ years.  That means each quarter people are cut, salaries never go up more than a percent, and there are insufficient resources to bring new products to market in a reasonable amount of time.

Pros: One of the best and most indepth training programs I could imagine. Great opportunity to build a solid foundation and core network before entering the field as a seller. You can take advantage of access to managers who will work to ensure you have a tailored experience prior to joining a fulltime team.
Cons: This is not necessarily a con, but the more selfmotivated and driven you are, the more success and opportunity you will gain from the program. Take advantage of the challenges to learn and grow professionally.

Pros: Great People  Pathway to change your career if you network and help people  I've had great managers  Opportunity to learn and develop skills outside of your job title  Love the Agile Floor!  My managers have kept me very informed on the politics of the business
Cons: Not many perks free coffee would be an instant moral booster  Moving away from Remote Work depends on perspective

Pros: Awesome work from home option, with numerous office locations to work from either permanently or occasionally. Decent access to office tools and applications. Lots of free training and upskilling options.
Cons: Complex work environment aggravated by matrixmanaged globally located teams with differing priorities and a constant need to validate their own department's existence. Quarterly resource actions.

Pros: Always had good people to keep things running.
Cons: Experienced people are let go, over time it has become harder and harder to find anyone with experience to keep things running.  IBM will spend a dollar to save a dime but won't spend money where it is needed to keep the infrastructure and experienced personnel.

Pros: I joined IBM after my MBA. They have a substantial 6month training program for client executives, where they teach you about consultative sales and IBM solutions. I impressed by my colleagues, the supportive/teamoriented culture and by the transformation taking place at the company.
Cons: There aren't many. They offer a very good compensation, benefits and worklife balance package for employees. The biggest challenge is the organization is large. Unfortunately, this takes time to get some things done, but over time you learn to manage through it.

Job Title: Portfolio Cloud And Saas Sales Representative
Pros: IBM as a company has been transforming itself over the last four years. They have invested a lot of time and money into making the world a better place around Watson Healthcare,
Cons: Because IBM is transforming and fighting to stay up with this volital industry. A lot of shuffling occurs annually to our Global Sales Teams, which could lead to clients frustration around loyalty.

Pros: The products and services are superb.  The coworkers are all wonderful, smart people.  The benefits are quite good too.
Cons: If you're over 40, your days are numbered.  Mass layoffs every 90 days, mostly targeting anyone over 40 who they will throw out the door with only one month of severance pay regardless of tenure.  You have to be employed on December 15th in order to get your 401k company match.  This is a toxic environment.  Upper management is only focused on feathering their own nest.  You've been warned about IBM.  If you get whacked its your own fault.

Pros: Access to large hardware resources for training machine learning models. Good training resources. Lots of smart coworkers to learn from.
Cons: Not working closely enough with groups outside the company on medical products. Functional groups within the company require product development groups to do quality assurance tasks before release without providing tools forcing the product development groups to recreate QA tools over and over again.

Pros: Competitive compensation. Room for upward movement. IBM has their hand in everything, so there are tons of opportunities to change what you're doing and grow. Free trainings to grow your skills.
Cons: Just have to survive the layoffs. As long as you can do that, the opportunities feel endless.

Pros: I worked at the company for 20 years. One of the reasons I stayed so long is that relative to other companies they walked the talk on diversity. I looked up and saw women and blacks in leadership roles. Perhaps there weren't as many as I would like but it was better than most companies and made me know moving up the food chain was possible for me.
Cons: The company moves very slowly and has far too much process. Not great for a more entrepreneurial person.

Pros: IBM is where you want to be if you are excited about being a part of the move to leading edge technology, working for a global leader of over 105 years, learning development, becoming an inventor, helping companies reach their operational and technological goals worldwide, and being part of an organization that makes a difference in the world. That's why you work for IBM. Because you have an Incredibly Brilliant Mind.
Cons: You need to commit time and effort.

Pros: A place where technically  no limits to grow. You can learn and do whatever you like.
Cons: Salaries to  many employees are below average. Promotion not well on time even for deserving candidates and performances many times are being totally overlooked.

Pros: Whether you're fresh out of college, or an experienced professional, IBM is the place to be. Here, you can cultivate your expertise, use your knowledge to the fullest extent, or reinvent yourself, without ever having to leave the company.
Cons: Such a large company. You can be lost as number even as an intern. The development and investment in the growth of the new interns did not meet my expectations.

Pros: IBM has a lot of employees that are loyal and have stayed with the company a long time. They offer very good benefits and are a long standing company. They are very professional and require high performance and professionalism.
Cons: IBM has yearly layoffs and the bonus structure and pay is very low compared to other technology companies. Opportunity for advancements are rare and the company does not have a hire within mentality. Much of the work is outsourced.

Job Title: Social And Digital Excperiencetechnical Sales Specialist
Pros: Super intelligent employees. Exciting new technologies like Watson are currently available and will change how we use computers forever.
Cons: Very bureacratic company. Politics within the organization are very tough. IBM recently reorganized all of its sales forces into specific functional areas. For some it is working out well and for others it has been a financial disaster with many not receiving commissions all year.

Job Title: I/T Specialist In Global Business Services, Band7
Pros: IBM has health benefits and vacation days, and many of the people I work with are top notch.
Cons: The vacation days will be hard to take due to demands of the job, and for every vacation day you do take, plan to work 8 hours unpaid overtime to make up your "utilization". The people who are Not top notch are incompetent at their work, and they make work for the top notch employees who are frustrated. Once hired do not expect more than a 1% raise and not every year.

Pros: The name on your resume  although that name is getting more and more tainted with all the bad news in the press about IBM.  Strong work from home culture.
Cons: Paralysed by process. IBM couldn't care less about their clients or their employees.  Poor pay. Don't even dream about getting a pay rise or bonus. No performance management or manager checkins to get feedback. Employee engagement data so poor that they don't share it with colleagues. If you do go into the office, you're lucky if they provide cups for water and paper towels!!! And buy your own coffee. And dish soap for the pantry!

Pros: IBM has a long technology history. It's a great place to work with incredible opportunity. The best thing about IBM is the incredibly talented folks working there.
Cons: IBM is struggling to reinvent itself to the cloud computing era. It has a massive hardware and software portfolio which needs to be retooled/revamped to be competitive in the current marketplace.

Pros: Talented people, thorough training, energetic leadership, mentorships, Summit hires are welcomed by all IBM employees and allowed to shadow and observe, sales and training curriculum is really well developed, management style is hands off and laid back, and company culture is work hard play hard.
Cons: A fair amount of travel involved with the Summit program. Workload can be intensive at times.

Job Title: App Integration And Middleware Solutions Specialist
Pros: Size:  Global Reach and working with peers all over the World Breadth:  Cloud Services, database Oracle, SQLServer, DB2, Cloudscape ...more, on Unix/Win./Mainframe, Websphere MQ, Tomcat, Websphere, Java, Web Services, XMLxsl ... and more
Cons: Size:  Institutional inertia and process bureaucracy can impede creativity and entrepreneurial spirit. Mgmt. layers:  Each can bring rulesets those under it must abide by.  Those at the endoftheline live under all if it.

Pros: Working from home!  IBM is a virtual company.  If you are a selfstarter and don't mind working from home, it allows for better office mates my dogs!.
Cons: Pay is not great, advancement opportunities are very limited.  Lots of bureaucratic administrative processes.

Pros: Paid a lot for doing absolutely nothing.
Cons: Doing absolutely nothing. They would pay travel expenses for me to go sit in a cafeteria at some client's office building for months at a time doing nothing, because the team I was on had about 8 people for 1person 20 hour/week worth of work. It was hilarious and hey free travel but I got zero relevant development experience for my 2 years working as a Java Developer. I literally didn't touch Java code once while there.

Pros: Good people and teams.  Many strong, well respected products.  Large install base across many solution areas.   Trying to catch amazon and Microsoft.
Cons: 15 quarters of decline says it all.  The brand has lost significant value as perceived by client decision makers.  The demand for IBM has dropped significantly.  Outsourcing and reduced staffing has hurt customer satisfaction and support.  Turnover is very high including senior leaders.  The cloud message isn't working.  Boosting cloud revenue through creative tactics.  Reduced compensation.

Job Title: Senior Cyber Threat Analyst And Cyber
Pros: One of the best things about working for IBM is the experience and working with high experience individuals. They let you think outside of the box to come up with different solutions and ideas.
Cons: for a con. it is a large company so it is easily for one to get lost in the shuffle and possible left behind.

Pros: My group was allowed to work remotely. Our team lead was great.
Cons: No training. No advancement. Had some awful managers but some good ones too. I was laid off when my account was offshored.

Pros: A lot of autonomy is given to employees to "get the job done"
Cons: IBM never shows a profit, so they are constantly restructuring the business model which cause frequent layoffs.  This is not a very positive way to reward employees who pour themselves into their work.

Pros: Learning opportunities and client variety keeps things very interesting in the IBM Consulting Business. Lots of gifted and smart people to work with on a daily basis.
Cons: Complex place to work. Ever changing business structures and movement of leaders makes it a bewildering environment to operate at times. Focus is on key client accounts and everyone is trying to sell into them via the lead client partners who determine who gets in to see whom at the client.

Pros: Great benefits, great environment, very good 1st line managers.
Cons: They stopped investing in their people, cut training, added ridiculous duplication to workloads. like multiple departments asking to fill out their form documenting your hours spent on customers. Everything went downhill and continued to after Lou Gerstner left the CEO position. I worked there long enough to see them reinvent the wheel and call it a 'new direction' they were taking.

Pros: Great benefits, acceptable pay, and flexibility with homelife balance issues. IBM, has an expansive ELearning platform to expand your skills, and education.
Cons: Within the area of development where I currently work there has been limited space for upward mobility for the past few years, I don't see it opening up any time soon.

Pros: Lots of opportunities to shift roles & learn new things, especially if you're trying to avoid being laid off. The best strategy is to switch teams/orgs every couple of years & hope yours isn't hit by reorg roulette.
Cons: Very old boy male dominated culture & vague "strategy". "Beat Microsoft" was our orgs marching orders. Very output/numbers oriented. They don't care what you do or if it's any good or even relevant, as long as you do a lot of whatever it is.

Pros: The best reasons to work for IBM are the competetive pay, community, and flexibility. As an intern, I am paid far beyond what most others my age with similar education are being paid. Very far beyond. IBM strives to create a sense of community, especially with interns who are being evaluated for possible fulltime hire. There are organized tours, classes, meetings, and events for interns and we are strongly encouraged to attend. IBM is also very fair and flexible when it comes to scheduled and unscheduled time off even for employees who are being paid hourly. Illness and emergency days have never been an issue.
Cons: Some of the downsides of working at IBM are the "nerd factor," the cultishness and arrogance of some employees, and the fact that the attempts to build community are sometimes overbearing. Most people who work at IBM are very nerdy and socially awkward, which can make them uncomfortable to be around and hard to communicate with. IBMers also fully believe that they are the best and their company is the best and that just because they are working at IBM they are somehow better than any other people in the technology field. Another downside is that sometimes IBM doesn't realize that employees have their own lives and friend and don't want to go to lunch, happy hour, and paintball with coworkers. There is sometimes pressure to attend optional activities outside of work hours.

Pros: Saying I worked for IBM for a year looks good on my resume.
Cons: Clunky, outdated virtual infrastructure; Excessive numbers of outsourced employees most of whom hardly speak English; Peeling paint, filthy walls and floors, broken plumbing with open sewage for over a year, no available drinking water in the building  For a multimillion dollar, international corporation, IBM has to be one of the 'cheapest' companies I've ever worked for.  Seriously, they'll even charge you for a napkin and a plastic fork in the employee break room!

Pros: IBM is a great organization to work for you if you are a selfstarter who can adapt to multiple request and changes.   There is opportunity to find new roles/jobs and try out new technologies.
Cons: Little opportunity for career growth  nearly zero mentoring or support unless you hunt it down yourself.   Continual focus and organizational changes.    Many jobs are posted on the internal job site  however they positions are being offered to candidates outside the company

Pros: Great exposure to new technologies e.g. Watson, cloud, collaboration. Working on multiple accounts showed varying perspectives in corporate culture and technological maturity from Fortune 100 companies to small businesses. 100% remote work  very flexible work/life balance.
Cons: Travel. Part of the job of an IBM architect is to sell IBM products and services, even if they are not the best fit. Funding for training and development is approved only if it is DIRECTLY related to supporting an account.

Pros: Flexibility has been great, but things are getting worse.  We just were told we had to move, or lose our job.
Cons: We have now been told we have to move or lose our job.

Pros: Iconic organization that has been involved since the dawn of computing.  IBM is filled with extremely bright, talented, and diverse teammates who are committed to building the future for the next 100 years.
Cons: Staying relevant with rate and pace of change in technology across the globe...has come with a price.  Transformation can bring the baggage of non productive pressures.

Pros: Large finance organization, plenty of opportunities to grow, great people to work with  this is IBM's biggest asset.
Cons: As with every shrinking company, a lot of pressure on expenses, headcount reductions IBM pays less than competitive rates, but if you get an external offer and "prove your market value" they will give you a counter offer.  Frequent reorgs keep the company in flux, make it hard for finance teams to develop and maintain measurement systems.

Pros: Amazing global opportunities, plethora of continuous learning with one of the greatest learning platforms, customized up and cross skilling in ground breaking / exponential technologies such as AI/Cognitive Computing, Blockchain, Big Data, IOT, Analytics, hybrid cloud, and cutting edge technologies such as quantum computing.
Cons: complex matrix management organization and too laborious to take any risks or business teams to make decisions.

Pros: When I worked at IBM, I was in need of assistance with some projects, and my coworkers were very helpful, and conscientious toward being team players. I was very grateful for the time I had to gain experience at IBM.
Cons: While there are some upper management that need to have their employment reevaluated, this company has a lot of people who want to help make things better, and I can appreciate that.

Pros: I love the flexibility that IBM gives us work balance work and life. They give you the space and are very understanding when life throws you a curve ball. The work opportunities are great and the people I work with are wonderful.
Cons: Being a large company IBM sometimes comes up with solutions that are not always the most efficient. Local management helps smooth this out though.

Pros: Global Name recognition for your resume Exposure to massive global implementation projects Ample opportunity for more trainings, certifications, etc Great Pay
Cons: Such a large company, sometimes you will fall through the cracks Difficult to climb the ladder. After a certain level at the company you completely plateau and cannot get promoted You are very replaceable in their eyes. They have 1000s of applications a day Dealing with old men in Technology with very old school methodologies, and are resistant to change

Pros: An inclusive company, in which everyone regardless gender, race, origin has the opportunity to grow. Solid career plan and incentive to make this happen. An open dialogue at the managerial level is essential for a good development and especially, to prevent small problems from becoming large. Especially after the pandemic, the human side has been taken much more into account. Great health insurance.
Cons: I do not consider the Profit Sharing Program a good benefit, it leave a lot to be desired

Pros: The fact that IBM has a creative learning system, where I enjoyed hands on training.
Cons: The disadvantage of working with IBM would be the length of time I shared with the company.

Pros: invest in a lot of training Great for parents with children, flexible telecommuting and good hours Compensation, you'll always get paid well here Great benefits, 401k match and full dental/medical Awesome, kind colleagues
Cons: A lot of time spent on reporting results in different formats than getting to do your job Internal tools are slow Not much work culture, working remote has its perks and disadvantages

Pros: Excellent coworkers, both socially and technically  Some very interesting work  Aboveaverage work environment
Cons: Overall direction sometimes drops "out of the sky".  Technical decisions swayed by outside groups. This can affect team focus.  Can be lots of "busy work" that doesn't seem connected with team goals. Granted, some is unavoidable in a large company, but still...

Pros: Best endtoend Technology capabilities and longterm solutions strategy.
Cons: Excellent sales training does not replace experience Crossfunctional promotions of marketing people to sales management, of direct sales to channel sales is an antiquated skills growth

Pros: The IBM legacy which is in serious danger of becoming only a distant memory.  This company has done great things in the past but has not learned to adapt to the market they seek to penetrate.
Cons: Dinosaur!  IBM will continue to lose market and relevance in all things they do until they get competent leadership and that flows down to competent middle management.  Process seems to be more important than results.  As a salesperson with a quota a was measured more on my ability to produce reports than on my sales numbers

Pros: Still a great company with tremendous resources, incredible people and a culture of focusing on the client.   The transition to new technology areas is exciting to be a part of.
Cons: IBM can be consuming with very high demands and expectations on personal time.  Decision making can be slow, but when IBM does decide on a strategic direction it typically goes all in.

Pros: In the sales organization they treat people decently.  It won't get fires for missing your quota once.  You will not be given too hard a time about using your vacation, but in sales expect that June and December are vacation nono's.
Cons: lack to real financial incentives to truely excel.  Socialization of pay.

Pros: The people I work with have high integrity and seek to put clients first. The values work IBM did a few years ago are making a difference. It's rewarding to work at a company that values: our clients success, innovation, and trust and responsibility in all relationships.
Cons: Too much focus on operational metrics.

Pros: Good benefits, nice name to have on your resume.  If you're young and have a MBA there are some good opportunities for you.
Cons: A lot of dead weight and company is very slow to respond to change.  Be prepared to spend too much time on calls with upper management tweaking your forecast and making your pipeline align to theirs.

Pros: The talent of people that you are able to work with in great and motivated.  You have the ability to gain customers attention and start a conversation easily by stating you are from IBM and I would like to talk to you about .....
Cons: Cumbersome processes which make you feel that you are not in control or that your view point matters.  Can not reach fast to customers questions and always need to set expectations that solutions or answers may take several days

Pros: Great People, ok processes and good in line classes
Cons: Churns through senior managers like butter. Pros: The benefits are good, starting at 3 wks a year plus up to 6 personal choice days.
Cons: You are expected even though the formal HR policy says not to to work through your dinner, vacations. You take your laptop everywhere  24x7. The company is quite matrixed and there is often disagreement about who handles what with sr mgmt deciding that "they" own a tactic, and another sr. mgmt says "he" handles it   you get caught in the middle  alot. The group owning the money for a tactic is not the same group implementing the tactic, this is why you see Web pages that don't make sense.  The advertising and direct mail tactic don't align to web pages, as a consumer, you are just "dropped." The best people have been laid off and the people left were personal favorites and not necessarily the right person for the job. Typically, the job was given to them without any training when the experienced person was laid off.  Layoffs have nothing to do with the quality  of work, they just got "too old" for IBM. That's how IBM beats the age discrimination rap, most of the laid off people are over 45 and subsequently high earners there's no getting around that. Turning 50 at IBM is the kiss of death. The best person that was laid off had much experience. IBM has not decided that experience doesn't mean anything and so they keep the inexperienced people, which explains why customers are frequently lost.  There is no loyalty to the employee. As a result of this, morale is very low, the hallways are quiet, there is no socializing, it's not a fun place to work.

Pros: IBM's pay and benefits were great.  They also had a strong commitment to worklife balance and actually encouraged workathome when it made sense.
Cons: Due to constant executive and management turnover and frequent reorgs, I felt  it was difficult  to establish the sort of reputation that I had developed at my prior company another IT equipment firm.    During my nearly 10 years at IBM, I was in senior positions in both software engineering and marketing.  While in SW engineering, I felt more like a cog in a machine than a respected professional.  For example, engineers seemed to get moved from projecttoproject without much thought about whether their technical background was a match for the new project.    Also, layoffs seemed to be more about being on the wrong project at the wrong time than about how good your engineering skills were.   CAVEAT: IBM is a big place, and I get the impression that it's not like this throughout IBM.  Also, I think the organization I was in has improved in that area since I left.  If you interview at IBM, ask the engineers how long they've been working on their particular project and how many projects/managers they've had in the last 23 years.   When I moved to marketing I was given good opportunity to advance and broaden, and I had reasonably good managers.  The biggest issue for me there was the fact that I had so many managers and had to work with so many different executives.  Someone once halfjoked, that if you don't like your manager, don't worry about it, you'll have a new one soon.   There were also a lot of reorgs.  All of this made it much  difficult to establish a reputation with upper management.  They simply didn't stay in one place long enough to get to know you.   At the executive level, it seemed that executives particularly the General Managers normally were hired for about a 23 year stint, then moved into another division.   As a result, they didn't seem interested in  strategy alternatives with longterm benefitsunless those options also provided shortterm payoffs that would occur on their watch.

What this means is that in the event you ask for an 8% raise over your current salary with your current employer, and they give it to you, when you start, that 8% will actually be null and void as they take that back to incentivize you over and above your agreed upon commissions numbers  it is a bait and switch in my opinion. Pros: The benefit packages that IBM provides are very good.  401k matching at 50% of the first 6%, and an automatic 2% contribution of your base pay into the plan whether you participate or not...IBM's way of eliminating a pension plan.
Cons: IBM doesn't care about their employee's welfare, and they will work you until you drop.  The only thing that really matters is your "utilization rate"...the higher the better...for IBM!  High utilization rates translates to more billable hours...but the average employee will never see a dime of that revenue...and your rate had better be north of 100%, or it will negatively impact your annual performance review.  Using any PTO also has a negative impact on your utilization rate since IBM is paying you, but cannot bill a client for your PTO.  So the only way to use PTO without a negative impact on your utilization is to essentially work a MINIMUM amount of unpaid overtime equal to the amount of PTO...and that's just to keep your utilization around 100%.  But true to the corporate greed model, there is ALWAYS a demand for utilization rates to be 108% or better...so you have to work MORE UNPAID OVERTIME than the amount of PTO used to have any chance at all of meeting the utilization targets.  Also, they manufacture these bogus "Quality and Innovation Summits", which is basically forced unpaid overtime on a weekend...and these QIS weekends ALWAYS seem to fall during a month where there is a Paid Holiday!!!  You'll get the Holiday off...with pay...but IBM will get their 8+ hours back!!!  And God forbid you come down off of an assignment in the January/February timeframe and hit the bench...IBM has their annual purge every February...like clockwork for the past 10 years...and if you're on the bench, there's a very good chance that you'll be out of a job in February.  My advice would be to STAY AWAY!  This once great company is a shell of its former self, and Thomas J. Watson has to be turning in his grave!!!

Cons: Bureaucracy can be a problem in such a large organisation and financial decision making is often based on global rather than local imperatives at times.

Pros: Good material: I have been given a 13in 2017 Macbook, at first it was a T460 ThinkPad  Very good CE: reimboursement of 40% of your travel invoice 3 invoices for hotel + train + car rental  BoisColombe Site is very spacious and beautiful; I work at Ecully, which is much smaller but still  convenient. Pros: I had some friends there. Oh and I no longer work there ;

Pros: I joined IBM in SAP Practice team with great expectation from both personal and professional point of view, and today i clearly call it out that it was right decision. Pros: I have worked for IBM 18 years. I have seen a lot of people go from this company to others in the industry Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, and others and the most common thing they miss about IBM is how much material to grow internally your skills is available.  Some other people miss the "good vibe", or the ethical principles by what we are guided... and this last part is no exageration, I have seen directly how top and executive management prefer to lose on a deal rather than winning it unethically. A big differentiator to some other companies in the industry.
Cons: IBM is a BIG company. And I mean BIIIG. Decisions, specially those that involve finance can take a lot of time, and work from the people involved. On the same note, career projection is also a long term goal. Planning your career in terms of the next 5 years is not uncommon, and is also a key difference, specially for younger employees.

Pros: contribution is not forced and it is up to the individual to contribute or sit back and relax or sometimes speak your way out without doing much
Cons: 1 No internal proper review cycle/system to judge a resource and grant them the package based on their performance and contribution towards the target. Resources are expected to prove themselves only by getting offer from other companies wherein, the panel would then work to match the package only to the fixed package, as they believe, that is the proof they got to judge the worth which is not ideal for a big company as it makes it look like they don't trust their resource enough with their own review mechanism 2 No rotation policy for support and development team career development is not considered 3 Company doesn't hesitate hiring a resource from outside for a hefty package, however thinks too much to nurture a good resource from within with reasonable hike cycles.

Pros: Such a huge company so the possibilities you have to develop yourself are big.
Cons: Too big. It's hard to be seen. Especially if working at CSO, the salaries are really different from the other ones known at IBM. Also , to get a promotion to a higher band, you must hardwork a lot for 100 or 200 reais more 50 to 100 USD. There are cases where the person was promoted and got only 50 reais 25 USD as salary plus food card with 150 reais 75 USD credit. Also it's really bad for all the CSO new employees to be employed with a 44hours week contract it means they work 40 and don't get any payment for the first 14 overtime hours worked, which is very very bad and unfair. About the retirement plan, IBM used to coparcipate with 3% + 50% of the employees contribuition, limited to 5%, which means that if the employee pays 10% or his/her salary, IBM used to pay 8% more to a fund. Now, all the new employees get only 1% from IBM. Nothing else. CSO seems to be different from the whole IBM.

Pros: Excellent 1st line managers who really care about their people. IBM Encourages movement across teams and projects, which keep skills and motivation fresh. Flexible working hours, and very openminded and supportive about work/life balance. I joined for longterm stability  which I got, but I believe times have been tougher since I left.
Cons: Annual peer reviews are overly beaurocratic and often a bit insulting  IBM seems to promote the team environment, but come annual assessment everyone is pitched against each other. I was even once told "you've had a great year, but I've got mark you as unsatisfactory, as I've got to draw the line somewhere". Tough times have seen a slash in all budgets, so very little in the way of rewards and off site team building. No education budget is tempered by highly skilled workforce doing skill shares. Once you get beyond the 1st line of management you often hit a wall of egos. In a long spell, I wasn't always impressed with 2nd line managers and above due to poor lines of communication, and the directors of engineering tended to throw their weight around unneccessarily. The work isn't always shared equally across teams  I noticed that often 90% of the work done is by 10% of the people.

Pros: Opportunity to travel although not always to glamorous locations High amount of flexibility between roles and ability to try different things. Ability to work from home some times.
Cons: Management and in fact all employees are overworked so nonessential activities like organizing team events, training and so on are often overlooked. Career development is left entirely to the employees who are told 'you are in control of your path'. I think that this is just laziness from management who really need to do more to guide and develop employees, especially ones that are new to the industry and don't understand the range of opportunities available,  Expectation to travel away from home and stay in a hotel every week Monday to Thursday. Long hours 50 hour week is completely normal and 60 hour week is not uncommon and people eat lunch at their desk rather than take a proper lunch break. IBM is not selling enough work, so there are not enough interesting projects, so the talented managers have left / are leaving, therefore the projects get in to problems due to weak leadership. This means that junior employees learn mostly from their own mistakes rather than good instructions from experienced managers, have to work really hard to grind out mediocre results, and do not get good job satisfaction from making clients happy.

Pros: salary, benefits, flex hours, friendly collegues
Cons: poor project planning,   poor coordination between teams,   weak management team, unable to strategically plan and coordinate resulting in chaos, which falls onto the backs of the developers to soft out and save the day and not be rewarded for that  poor hiring standards low competency  managers rarely care about people they manage, professional assessments are arbitrary   degree of professionalism is low, IBM used to have a very strong engineering and innovation leadership, not anymore  it dissipated in the last 810 years; uses 20 year technologies, slow to adopt new things  does not reward passion, in many cases managers of the type "steal the credit, shift the blame", environment tends to get political  keeps cutting essential services  HR, IT are cut and moved to a site in a different city  work is boring  environment is gender bias   very bureaucratic   lots of process overhead e.g. annual recertifications "how not to get bribed" trainings   talent is fleeing the company

Pros: IBM Support structures are second to none.  Cutting edge technologies, and innovations.
Cons: Lack of motivation from staff who are seeing nothing in the way of pay rises. Effectively having to take an inflation rate pay cut, year on year.  A review system that concentrates on performace metrics which are outdated, and inefectual, meaning that the people who get on with management get the best reviews, whilst those that actually DO the work are often not rewarded at all.

Pros: for IBM is not an employer its where my heart and soul are. its a place I look forward each day to interact, collaborate, learn, face new challenges with brilliant IBMers and Win battles for Clients and win their hearts. Each day is a learning because the people are so knowledgeable and helpful.
